prose.text: TITLE, Moses. See Ap. 2. Numbers. Translation of Greek name in Sept. given by man according to his idea of contents. Heb. Title = B'midbar = "in the wilderness", because it records what took place there; the numberings (1-3 and 26) being only two of the events. It is the book of the sojournings, the fourth book of the Pentateuch (see Ap. 10 and Deut. 1. 1). Four is the number of the earth: hence the types of Numbers, the fourth book, are wilderness types (cp. the fourth book of the Psalms, 90-106). Its types of Christ, the Son of Man on earth, are four:— (1) Bread of life, 11. 7-9 (John 6. 57, 58). (2) Water of life, 20. 11 (1 Cor. 10. 4). (3) Lifted up, 21. 9 (John 3. 14, 15). (4) The coming star out of Jacob, 24. 17 (Luke 1. 78. 2 Pet. 1. 19. Rev. 2. 28; 22. 16).

1. 1—4. 49 (A1, p. 176). NUMERATION AND ORDER OF SERVICE, &c. (Alternation). 1. 1-54. [For Structure see next page.] AND. Numbers begins with "And", as all the books of the Pentateuch do. It is therefore one whole in five sections, rather than separate books. the LORD spake = Jehovah (the Covenant God) spake to His own People. He spake fifty-six "sundry times" (7 x 8) in Numbers, and in thirteen "divers manners" (twelve to Moses, once to Aaron), and four times indefinite:— (1) To Moses alone (1. 1, 48; 3. 5, 11, 14, 44; 4. 21; 7. 4; 8. 5, 23; 10. 1; 11. 25; 13. 1; 16. 44; 25. 10, 16; 26. 52; 27. 6; 31. 1, 25; 34. 16. (2) To Moses, to speak to Aaron (8. 1). (3) To Moses, to speak to Aaron and his sons (6. 22). (4) To Moses, to speak to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest (16. 36). (5) To Moses, to speak to the Levites (18. 25). (6) To Moses, to speak to the congregation (16. 23). (7) To Moses, to speak to the children of Israel (5. 1, 5, 11; 6. 1; 9. 1 (cp. v. 4), 9; 15. 1, 17, 37; 17. 1; 28. 1 (cp. v. 2); 33. 50; 34. 1; 35. 1, 9). (8) To Moses, to speak to the rock (20. 7). (9) To Moses and Aaron (2. 1; 4. 1, 17; 14. 26; 16. 20; 20. 12, 23). (10) To Moses and Aaron, to speak to the children of Israel (19. 1). (11) To Moses and Aaron and Miriam (12. 4). (12) To Moses and Eleazar (26. 1). (13) To Aaron (18. 8). (v. 20 should be "said".) (14) Jehovah spake (indefinite) (1. 19; 3. 1; 14. 35; 27. 23). For "the LORD said", see note on 3. 40 (sixteen times, making seventy-two in all). Sinai. To which they had come on the third month after the exodus (Ex. 19. 1), and where they abode till the twentieth day of the second month of the second year (Num. 10. 11). The numbering (ch. 1) began on the first day of that month (v. 18). tabernacle = tent (Heb. 'ohel). See Ap. 40. come = gone.

Take ye. Cp. Ex. 30. 11, 12; 38. 25. In Exodus, moral law (prophet); Leviticus, ritual law (priest); Numbers, commonwealth law (king). sum. Three numberings. Ex. 30. 11, 12 (cp. 38. 25, 26); here; and 26. congregation. See note on Gen. 28. 3. children = sons. Heb. banim, from banah, to build, because the family thus built up. Cp. Gen. 30. 3. Ruth 4. 11. So throughout. polls. Edition of 1611 = poll. Fig. Synecdoche (of Part), Ap. 6, skull or head put for person.
thou and Aaron. In second numbering it is Moses and Eleazar, 26. 1.
man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. every tribe. Hence twelve, and, with Moses and Aaron, fourteen. So the twelve apostles, with Paul and Barnabas = fourteen.

these are the names. The order here = five sons of Leah, three of Rachel, one of Bilhah, two of Zilpah, and one of Bilhah. See Ap. 45 for other orders of the names. men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. See Ap. 14.
Nahshon. In the line of the promised seed, the father of Salmon (husband of Rahab of Jericho), progenitor of Boaz of Bethlehem (husband of Ruth). Cp. Ruth 4. 18-22. Matt. 1. 4, 5. Luke 3. 32.
As = according as. wilderness of Sinai (v. 1), to distinguish it from the second, which was in the plains of Moab.
Reuben. Lost his dignity in Gen. 49. 3, 4; not many in number here. eldest son. See Ap. 45.

Simeon was greatly diminished by sin in Num. 26. 4, and Moses does not mention him in Deut. 33. Those that were numbered of them. Some codices, with two early printed editions, Onk., Jon., Sept., and Syr., omit this clause. Cp. vv. 20, 24, 26, &c.
Gad takes the place of Levi here.
fifty. Gad is the only one who has "tens", all the others "hundreds". In the case of the firstborn (3. 43) we have not only tens but units.
Judah. His number is greatest (Gen. 49. 8).

Joseph. "The fruitful vine" (Gen. 49. 22) has two tribes (not merely "families"). Thus Joseph has "the double portion" (1 Chron. 5. 1, 2). Ephraim. Blessed first (Gen. 48. 19, 20), is here named first, and is increased more than Manasseh (Deut. 33. 17). But in journeyings his numbers were diminished by 8,000. See 26. 37, and cp. 1 Chron. 7. 20-22.
Manasseh. The lowest in number. See Gen. 48. 19. Increased by 20,500 in journeying, 26. 34, 37 (cp. Job 12. 23).

Of the children. So in A.V., and R.V., but not in Heb. text, though it is so in some codices, Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg. Some Jewish commentators explain it as being only "the sons", because Naphtali had more daughters than sons, and in Gen. 49. 51 is likened to a female (hind). Hence in 26. 64 it is said, the "men" died (but the women multiplied).
twelve men: one man for one tribe (v. 4). men. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.

all they. The number in Ex. 12. 37 is not "exaggerated", as the number here had increased since then; moreover, the numbers here coincide with the numbers of the half-shekels, which had been contributed by them in Ex. 30. 14 and 38. 25, 26, before the tabernacle was set up. Cp. Ex. 38. 25 with 40. 17.
Levites not numbered here with the nation, but separately in 3. 14-29.
spoken. See note on 1. 1.
tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. See Ap. 40.
put to death. Probably by Jehovah. Cp. 1 Chron. 13. 10.
camp: to be set forth in detail in member B, below.
pitch = encamp. that there be no wrath: i.e. no judgment from God. "wrath" put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause) for the judgment inflicted. Ap. 6. Heb. kazaph. First occurrence.
2. 1-34 (B, p. 177). ORDER OF ENCAMPMENT. (Introversion and Repeated Alternation.) the LORD [Heb. Jehovah] spake. See note on 1. 1.

man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. children = sons. See note on 1. 2. pitch = encamp. standard. Heb. degel. ensign. Each standard is said to have had as its "sign" one of the twelve constellations (see note on Gen. 1. 16, and Ap. 12. Heb. 'oth) depicted on it. One standard, with its sign on it for each tribe. Hence called "ensign". See notes on the tribes below, from the Targum of Jonathan. far off = over against. Same as Ps. 38. 12, yet so as to be in view. Cp. 2 Kings 2. 7. Deut. 32. 52. Gen. 21. 16. tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40.

east. The order proceeds according to the course of the sun: east, south, west, north. camp. Each camp composed of three tribes. Cp. vv. 3, 10, 17, 18, 25, 32. Judah. The sign, a lion (Gen. 49. 9. Ezek. 1. 10. Rev. 4. 7). The standard, the colours of the three stones of the second row, Ex. 28. 18. For the order, see Ap. 45.
Issachar, brother of Judah (same mother, Leah). Gen. 35. 23. Sign on standard = Cancer.
Then. This word, according to some codices, with Sam., should not be in italics. Cp. vv. 14, 22, 29. Zebulun, brother of Judah (same mother, Leah). Gen. 35. 23. Sign on standard = Virgo.
south. See note on "east", v. 3. Reuben. The centre of the south side, with standard in the colours of stones of first row of Ex. 28. 17; and sign, a man (Gen. 30. 14) = Aquarius in Zodiac.
Simeon, the brother of Reuben (same mother, Leah). Gen. 35. 23. Sign = Pisces.

Gad, brother of Reuben (same mother, Leah). Gen. 35. 23. Sign = Aries. Reuel. Some codices, with one early printed edition, Onk., Jon., and Vulg., have "Deuel", as in ch. 1. 14; 7. 42; 10. 20; the R (Resh, R) being mistaken for D (Daleth, D). Probably called, indifferently, by either name.

tabernacle of the congregation. See note on v. 2. This was in centre. So is the tent of the chief of the tribe to this day. The manner of its being carried is shewn in ch. 10. 17, &c. Levites. The order of the Levites' camping is shown in ch. 3, their marching in ch. 10. Their sign was Libra, or more anciently the "altar". as = according as.

west. See note on v. 3. Heb. = sea, that being west. Ephraim. The centre on the west side. The colours of the stones in fourth row of Ex. 28. 20. The sign, an ox (Deut. 33. 17. Ezek. 1. 10. Rev. 4. 7). In the Zodiac, Ephraim and Manasseh are the two horns of Taurus, the bull. Ephraim, the younger, bears the standard, according to the blessing in Gen. 48. 14-20.
Manasseh, brother of Ephraim by same mother (Gen. 41. 51, 52). Sign, see v. 18.
Benjamin, sons of Rachel, all on west side. Sign, Gemini.

Dan. The centre on the north side. Colours of standard same as those of the third row of stones in Ex. 28. 19. Sign, the eagle (substituted for the serpent of Gen. 49. 17). Cp. Ezek. 1. 10. Rev. 4. 7.
north. See note on v. 3.
Asher, the son of the other handmaid Zilpah, put with Dan and Naphtali, the sons of Bilhah. His sign was Sagittarius, the Archer.
Naphtali. His sign was Capricornus, the goat. Cp. Gen. 49. 21.

the camps. See note on v. 3, and Ap. 45. They may be thus set forth:— EAST. Issachar (Cancer). Judah (Leo). Zebulon (Virgo). Naphtali (Capricornus). Dan (Scorpio, Eagle). Asher (Sagittarius). Moses, Aaron, and the Priests. Merarites. Kohathites. Gershonites. Simeon (Pisces). Reuben (a Man). Gad (Aries). Benjamin (Gemini). Ephraim (Taurus). Manasseh. WEST.

3. 1-51 (A, p. 177). NUMERATION OF THE LEVITES. generations. The twelfth occurrence (eleven in Genesis (see p. 1), one here, one in Ruth 4. 18-22, one in Matt. 1. 1, fourteen (2 x 7, see Ap. 10) in all. the LORD = Jehovah, Israel's Covenant God. See Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.
These. Some codices, with one early printed edition, Sam., Onk., and Syr., read "And these". whom he consecrated. See note on Ex. 28. 41.
died before the LORD. This parenthetical statement is an undesigned coincidence referring to Lev. 10. 1-7. Cp. Num. 26. 61, and 1 Chron. 24. 2. children = sons.
present = cause it to stand.
tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40. the tabernacle. Heb. mishkan. Ap. 40.
instruments = vessels or furniture. Israel. The whole nation was responsible for this charge, but Levi was taken in substitution for the firstborn. Cp. vv. 38, 41, and cp. 8. 16. Ex. 13. 11-16.
wholly given. Heb. "given, given". Fig. Epizeuxis (Ap. 6), for emphasis. Hence called n'thunim = given ones.
11-51 [For Structure see next page].
11-51 (k, p. 181). LEVITES SUBSTITUTED FOR THE FIRSTBORN (Introversion). behold. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6), for emphasis.

hallowed = separated. See note on "holy", Ex. 3. 5. man. Heb. 'adam. See Ap. 14. i. I am the LORD. This is the reason for this act of sovereignty. Cp. Ex. 12. 29, 30; 13. 2. The interpretation of Heb. 12. 23 depends on this ordinance. Note the emphatic "I", v. 12, and the Fig. Asterismos there.
word. Heb. "mouth", put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for words spoken by it. as = according as.
names. Substituted by name here because redeemed by name. Ex. 1. 1.
the. Some codices, with Sam., Onk., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and the" door = entrance.
candlestick = lampstand.
chief over the chief. Heb. = "chief of the chief". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), being a kind of Enallage (Ap. 6).
Merari. Fig. Epanadiplosis (Ap. 6), the verse beginning and ending with the same word.
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton in vv. 36, 37 (Ap. 6), to emphasise each item mentioned.
charge of the children of Israel. The whole nation responsible. Cp. vv. 8 and 41, 45.

and Aaron. These two words are dotted in the Hebrew. See Ap. 31. The command was given to Moses alone (vv. 14, 15), and was carried out by him alone (v. 16). As Aaron took part, according to 1. 3, 4, and 4. 41, 45, 46, his name was included here by some ancient copyist; and later scribes dotted the words rather than leave them out. commandment. Heb. "mouth", put for what was spoken by it by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6.

the LORD said = Jehovah said. Heb. 'amar (not davar, spake). 'amar is followed by the words spoken, davar is not. This expression, Jehovah said, occurs eighteen "sundry times" and in five "divers manners" in this book of Numbers. Cp. note on 1. 1 (1) To Moses (alone), 3. 40; 7. 11; 11. 16, 23; 12. 14; 14. 11; 15. 35; 17. 10; 21. 8, 34; 25. 4; 27. 12, 18. (2) To Aaron, 18. 1. (3) To Balaam, 23. 5, 16. (4) He said, 12. 6. (5) I Jehovah have said, 14. 35. With the fifty-six times "Jehovah spake" (see 1. 1), these eighteen make seventy-four times, and sixteen manners. See note on 22. 9, for "God said" (four times, making seventy-eight in all).
as = according as
instead. This substitution is the subject of this large member.
redeemed = bought back. Heb. g'aal. See note on Ex. 6. 8 more = over and above: 273 (= 13 x 21). Ap. 10. The firstborn males were 22,273; The Levites were 22,000; difference 273.
shekels. See Ap. 51. II. gerahs. See Ap. 51. II.
of = from.
a thousand, &c. = 1365 (= 13 x 105), being 5 x 273, i.e. five shekels apiece, v. 47. See Ap. 10.
4. 1-49 (B, p. 177). LEVITES: THE ORDER OF THEIR SERVICE. (Introversion.) 1-33 (n, above). THE COMMAND (GIVEN). (Repeated Alternation.) the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

thirty. This thirty pertains to their numbering. The age twenty-five pertains to their service. So that there was a probationary five years. Changed (by Divine direction given to David) in 1 Chron. 23. 23, 24, 27 to twenty. Cp. 2 Chron. 31. 17. all that enter into the host. This expression occurs five times in this chapter, vv. 3, 30, 35, 39, 43. tabernacle of the congregation = "tent of meeting". Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40.
most holy = the holiest. Heb. holiness of holinesses. See note on Ex. 3. 5.
And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), here and in following verses, to emphasise each particular in vv. 5-15.
table of shewbread. See Ex. 25. 30 and Lev. 24. 6. dishes. In chap. 4 rendered "charger" throughout. spoons = dishes. bowls = pans. covers = bowls. to cover = to pour. continual. Cp. Lev. 24. 8.
candlestick = light-holder, as in Gen. 1. 14.
bar = pole. Cp. 13. 23.

the. Some codices, with Sam., Onk., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and the". See note on v. 5 above. fleshhooks: or forks. and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), emphasising each separate item. basons: or sprinkling-bowls.
holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5.
light = candlestick. See on v. 9 above. tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. Ap. 40
every one = each to his own work. No confusion.
to see. Cp. Ex. 19. 21. 1 Sam. 6. 19.
perform the service. Heb. war the warfare. Fig Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis = do the important or solemn work.
door = entrance.
appointment. Heb. "mouth", put for what is said or bidden by it. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6.
do the work. Heb. "serve the service". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis = perform the solemn service.
the instruments of. Instead of these words some codices, with Sam., Jon., and Sept., read "all", i.e. "all the charge".
34-45 (o, p. 183). OBEDIENCE. (Repeated and Extended Alternation.)
commandment. Heb. "mouth". Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, put for words spoken by it. hand. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, "hand" put for ministry performed by Moses.
46-49 (n, p. 183). COMMAND (COMPLETED). (Extended Alternation.) (Compare the above with "o", above.)
do the service. Heb. "serve the service". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis = do the solemn or important service.

commandment. Heb. "mouth", put for what is said by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6. hand. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for ministry performed by it. every one. Heb. 'ish 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii.

5. 1—9. 23 [For Structures see next page]. 5. 1—9. 23 (B1, p. 176). LAWS AND EVENTS. (Alternation and Introversion.) 5. 1—6. 21 (a, above). LAWS FOR THE PEOPLE. 5. 1-31 (c1, above). NECESSARY LAWS. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

children = sons. See note on 1. 2. the dead = the soul. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13. Cp. ch. 6. 6. Lev. 21. 1. Num. 19. 11. See note on Lev. 19. 28. Touching a dead man, rendered the one who touched unclean seven days (19. 11); touching other dead creatures, rendered unclean only till the evening (Lev. 11. 27, 39, 40).
put out, without the camp. Cp. 12. 14, 15.
as = according as.
man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. sin. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i. men. Heb. 'adam. See Ap. 14. i. trespass. Heb. ma'al. Ap. 44. xi. person = soul. Heb. nephesh. (Ap. 13.)
recompense = return back. trespass. Heb. 'asham. Ap. 44. ii.
kinsman. Heb. goel, redeemer. See note on Ex. 6. 6. atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33.
offering = heave offering. Heb. t'rumah. See Ap. 43. viii., and note on Ex. 29. 27. holy = separated. See note on Ex. 3. 5.
hallowed = separated. See note on "holy", Ex. 3. 5. whatsoever. Some codices, with one printed edition, Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and whatsoever". his: i.e. the priest's.
11-31 (d3, above). JEALOUSY (Repeated Alternation).
the spirit of jealousy = a jealous motion or affection of the mind. Here, Heb. ruach (Ap. 9) is put for the feelings, &c., as in Isa. 11. 2. Eph. 1. 17. Hos. 4. 12.

offering. Heb. korban, approach-offering. See Ap. 43. II. i. ephah. See Ap. 51. III. 3. barley. No other grain, and no other measure. Cp. Lev. 2. 1. offering: i.e. of jealousy. Heb. minchah (Ap. 43. II. iii.), meal offering. offering: i.e. of memorial. i.e. causing iniquity to be remembered. iniquity. Heb. 'avah. Ap. 44. iv.
holy = separated: taken from the laver. See note on Ex. 3. 5. tabernacle. Heb. mishkan. Ap. 40.
bitter water. Heb. water of bitters, Genitive of cause: i.e., causing bitterness of spirit. Cp. Ps. 109. 18. Prov. 5. 4. Bitter = ham'arim. curse. Fig. Paronomasia (Ap. 6). Heb. ham'arim.
charge, &c. This ordeal was provided for in the Laws of Khammurabi, §§ 131, 132. See Ap. 15.
Amen. A Hebrew word, transferred to the Greek—verily, truly so. If one adjured another and he replied "Amen", it was thereby considered as confirmed by an oath. Cp. 2 Cor. 1. 20.
become bitter = turn to bitterness.
offering. Heb. minchah, gift or meal offering. See Ap. 43. II. iii. wave. See note on Ex. 29. 27. offer it = bring it. Heb. karab. Ap. 43. I. i.
memorial. The handful (Lev. 2. 2) so-called. burn. Heb. katar. See Ap. 43. I. vii.
be. Heb. she be.
iniquity. Heb. 'avah. Ap. 44. iv. bear her iniquity = bear the punishment of it. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6. Cp. Lev. 20. 17, 19, 20. Ezek. 4. 4, 5. See Ap. 44. iv.

6. 1-21 (c2, p. 186). VOLUNTARY (NAZARITE VOW) (Alternation). Note the order in these laws: (1) separation, 6. 1-12; (2) worship, 6. 13-21; (3) blessing, 6. 22-27; (4) service, 7. 1-89. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

children = sons. man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. woman. Either could be a Nazarite. vow a vow. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis = make a special vow. Cp. Acts 18. 18; 21. 23. a Nazarite = one separate, from Heb. nazir, to separate. Cp. Gen. 49. 26. Judg. 13. 5, 7. Lam. 4. 7.
wine. Heb. yayin. See Ap. 27. i. strong drink. Heb. shekar. See Ap. 27. iv. liquor of grapes = mashed grapes. moist = green or "fresh".
separation = Nazariteship. vine tree = grape vine.
come at = come near. no dead body = no dead soul. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13, and note on Lev. 19. 28.
consecration = separation, or Nazariteship. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.
turtles = turtle-doves. door = entrance. tabernacle of the congregation = tent of assembly. See Ap. 40.

offer = prepare. See Ap. 43. I. iii. atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33. dead = soul. Heb. nephesh (Ap. 13): i.e. the dead person. hallow his head: i.e. by beginning anew the days of his vow (v. 9), during which the hair must grow, as in v. 5. See note on "holy", Ex. 3. 5.
consecrate = separate. separation = Nazariteship. trespass offering. See Ap. 43. II. vi. be lost. Heb. fall, i.e. not be counted.
the Nazarite = the one separate.
offer = bring near. Heb. karab. See Ap. 43. I. i. offering = approach offering. Ap. 43. II. i. sin offering. See Ap. 43. II. v.
cakes = pierced cakes. meat offering = meal or gift offering. Ap. 43. II. iii.
sacrifice. Ap. 43. I. iv. and II. xii.; cp. Acts 21. 26, 27.
sodden = boiled.
wave offering. See note on Ex. 29. 27. holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5.
beside, &c.: i.e., if able, he might voluntarily make an addition thereto.
22-27 (b, p. 186). THE PRIESTS' LAW. BLESSING. A triple blessing of three members, from Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. See Ap. 10.
Aaron and unto his sons. Cp. Deut. 21. 5. 1 Chron. 23. 13. bless. Deut. 10. 8.
The LORD = Jehovah the Father, the source of all blessing. Cp. Eph. 1. 3. Heb. 10. 7.
The LORD = Jehovah the Son, the channel of all blessing, Eph. 1. 3. Cp. Acts 3. 26. Heb. 10. 10. face: put by Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), for whole Person. Ap. 6. Also Fig. Anthropopatheia.

The LORD = Jehovah the Spirit, the witness of all blessing. Cp. Heb. 10. 7, 10, 15. countenance: same as "face" in v. 25: this is the token of Divine favour and delight. Cp. Job 29. 24. Ps. 4. 6, and the result v. 7. peace = rest or security.
7. 1-89 (D, p. 186). DEDICATION OF THE ALTAR (Alternation). tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. Cp. Ex. 40. 18. See Ap. 40.
the princes. Though their offerings were the same as the others, yet each is recorded separately. offered = brought near. Heb. karab. Ap. 43. I. i.
brought. Same as "offered", v. 2. offering = approach offering. Heb. korban. Ap. 43. II. i. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
4-9 [For Structure see next page]. spake. See note on 1. 1.

4-9 (F, p. 188). ARRANGEMENT. (Alternation.) do the service. Heb. serve the service. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis = perform the solemn service. tabernacle of the congregation = tent of assembly. See Ap. 40. man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii.
11-89 (F, p. 188). ARRANGEMENT. (Division.) said. See note on 3. 40.
tribe. The order is the same as in ch. 2. See Ap. 45.
shekels. See Ap. 51. II. meat offering = gift offering. See Ap. 43. II. iii.
One. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "And one".
children = sons.
One. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "And one". sin. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i.
Deuel = Deguel, in ch. 2. 14 = Reguel. See note there, and cp. 1. 14.
sacrifice. Heb. zabah. Ap. 43. xii.
in the day: i.e. in the twelve days. See Ap. 18.
tabernacle of the congregation. Heb. tent of meeting. See Ap. 40. with Him: i.e. with Jehovah. Cp. v. 11. mercy seat. See note on Ex. 25. 17.
8. 1-26 (C b, p. 186). LAWS FOR THE PRIESTS AND LEVITES (Repeated Alternation). the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.
the = the face of the. candlestick = light-holder (as in Gen. 1. 14), or lampstand. Cp. Ex. 25. 31-39; 37. 17-24.
as = according as.
unto. Some codices, with Sam., Onk. MS., and Jon., read "and unto".
children = sons.
water of purifying = sin water: i.e., water prepared as in ch. 19.
meat offering. See Ap. 43. II. iii. sin offering. See Ap. 43. II. v.
tabernacle of the congregation = tent of meeting. Ap. 40.
offer. Heb. wave. See note on Ex. 29. 27. offering. Heb. wave offering. See Ap. 43. II. ix. execute the service. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6). Heb. "serve the service" = perform the solemn service.
the Levites. Fig. Epanadiplosis (Ap. 6), the verse beginning and ending with the same word. offer = prepare. Heb. 'asah. Ap. 43. I. iii. atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33.
Mine. Cp. 3. 45.
offer them for an offering = wave them for a wave offering. See Ex. 29. 27.
For. Cp. Ex. 13. 2. Num. 3. 13. man. Heb. 'adam. See Ap. 14. i. on the day. See Ap. 18.
as = according as.

twenty and five years old. This was the commencement of a five years' probation. The age, thirty, was the age of their numbering. See note on 4. 3. to wait, &c. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), as in vv. 11, 15, 19. Lit. war the warfare.
from the age, &c. Observe the gracious care of Jehovah.

9. 1-14 (a, p. 186). LAWS FOR THE PEOPLE. (Introversion.) the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1. During the week of Aaron's consecration, Abib 1-8. first month, &c. Therefore before the numbering which was on the first day of the second month (1. 1, 2). The observance mentioned here in connection with the second passover, a month later (vv. 6-11).
children = sons.
kept the passover: the second of ten recorded. See note on Ex. 12. 18, 28. Lev. 23. 5. Num. 28. 16. Deut. 16. 2, and cp. 7. 89—9. 14.

men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh, Ap. 14. ii. Probably Mishael and Elizaphan, who had buried Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10. 1-4); they were thus rendered unclean, and could not keep the passover (Num. 19. 11; 5. 2). by = for touching. body = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. man. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. i.
any man. Heb. 'ish, 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. body = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. afar off. In Heb. MSS. dotted, to show these words are to be omitted. See Ap. 31. Distance not limited.
second month. Therefore a month later than the appointed day (v. 1).
man. Heb. 'enosh. Ap. 14. iii. soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. offering = approach offering. Heb. korban. Ap. 43. II. i.
9. 15-23 (D, p. 186). EVENT. ERECTION OF TABERNACLE (Repeated Alternation). tabernacle = habitation. Heb mishkan. Ap. 40. was = came to be: i.e. remained.
tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40.
At the, &c. Fig. Epibole. Ap. 6, repeated. commandment. Heb. mouth. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6; mouth put for command given by it.
a few days. Heb. "days of number": i.e. days easily counted. according to, &c. Fig. Mesarchia, Ap. 6 (twice).
abode. Cp. Ex. 40. 34-38.
At the commandment, &c. Fig. Epibole Ap. 6. hand = mediation, or ministry; "hand" put by Fig Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6.
10. 1-36 (A2, p. 176). JOURNEYINGS AND ORDER (MARCH) (Repeated Alternation). the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

two: here only two. Later, 120 (2 Chron. 5. 12). trumpets. These were of two principal kinds: those called chazoz'rah, made of silver, and straight; the other, shophar, a horn. These must be distinguished. The other words are yobel, a jubilee horn (Ex. 19. 16); and tako'a, the blast of a trumpet (Ezek. 7. 14). of a whole piece = of beaten work. use them: for four purposes: (1) assembly; (2) journeying; (3) for war; (4) for the feasts. assembly = whole congregation: i.e. in its civil character.
door = entrance. tabernacle of the congregation = tent of meeting. Ap. 40.
blow. Heb. teru'ah = a prolonged blowing.
congregation = assembly = a portion only, in its military character.
sons. Cp. Lev. 1. 5.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.

solemn days = appointed seasons. Between vv. 10 and 11 comes in the account of Jethro, Ex. 18. See Deut. 1. 7-14, where the choosing of judges takes place after Horeb, but is recorded in Ex. 18 before Horeb. See note on Ex. 18.
twentieth day, &c. See Ap. 50. vii. 3. tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. Ap. 40.
children = sons. took their journeys. Heb. idiom, "journeyed for their journeyings" = set forward. On 20th of Ziph, 1490, and ended 10th Abib 1451. Lasted 38 years and 15 days.
commandment. Heb. mouth. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6; "mouth" put for what is spoken by it.
the first place. For the order of the twelve tribes, see Ap. 45. camp. Note distinction between "camp" and "host". Cp. 2. 3. Nahshon. Cp. 1. 7; 2. 3.
Deuel, called also Reuel, 2. 14.
the other: i.e. the Gershonites and Merarites. See v. 17.
Raguel, called also Reuel (Ex. 2. 18).
mount of the LORD = mountain of Jehovah: because His glory had there been revealed. three days. From 20-23 Ziph. Ap. 50. VII. 3.
Read this verse after v. 36. See following note.

35, 36. These two verses are marked Heb. MSS. by "inverted Nuns", i.e. the Heb. letter (n) inverted and used as brackets, to show that vv. 35 and 36 are thus enclosed to show that v. 34 should follow v. 36. This is shown by the Structure:— [see the diagram "10. 33-36. The Inverted Nuns"] There are eight of these inverted nuns. See notes on Ps. 107. 23-28. Rise up. A beautiful prayer. Cp. Ps. 3. 7; 7. 6; 10. 12; 17. 13; 44. 26; 68. 1.
Return. Either, Return, O Jehovah; or, Cause to return. Cp. Deut. 30. 3. Ps. 14. 7; 126. 1. The former better. Cp. Ex. 33. 14-16.

11. 1—25. 18 (B2, p. 176). EVENTS AND LAWS. (Repeated Alternation.) 11. 1—14. 45 (L1, above). EVENTS. 11. 1—12. 16 (N1, above). MURMURINGS AND JOURNEYINGS (Alternation). 11. 1-34 (r. above). MURMURINGS OF PEOPLE. (Alternation.) complained. Heb. were as complainers, Ps. 78. 19. In this word another inverted nun (n), to mark the fact of the People's turning back in their hearts. See note on 10. 35. it displeased the LORD. Heb. "was evil in the ears of Jehovah". Some codices, with Onk., Jon., Sept., and Syr., read "eyes" instead of "ears". the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. II. the fire. Those before the Law not punished, Ex. 14. 11-15; 15. 24-26; 16. 2-4, 9, 20, 27, 28; 17. 2-4. Punished after Law given. Ex. 32. 27-35. Cp. Rom. 4. 15.
he called: i.e. Moses called. the place = that place. Taberah. Heb. "burning".

4-34 (u, p. 195). MURMURING AND PLAGUE. (Repeated Alternation.) multitude = camp followers. See Ex. 12. 38. fell a lusting. Heb. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. = "lusted a lusting", emphatic for lusted exceedingly. Ps. 106. 14; 78. 18-20. children = sons. Who shall give? Fig. Erotesis (Ap. 6).

the fish. Six items given of Egypt's food: seven of Canaan's, in Deut. 8. 8. See Ap. 10. freely = gratuitously. and. Note Fig. Polysyndeton in this verse (Ap. 6), to emphasise the six items. See v. 8.
our soul is. Heb. nephesh = we [are]. Ap. 13.
manna. Cp. John 6. 31-33. 1 Cor. 10. 3. colour. Heb. "eye", put by Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, for that which it distinguishes. Ex. 16. 14, 31.
dew fell. Manna between the two dews, cp. Ex. 16. 13, 14.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. door = entrance. Moses also was displeased = it was evil in Moses' eyes, as in v. 1.
Wherefore, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
bosom. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. as = even as.
Whence, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
it is = the burden is. The Ellipsis to be supplied according to Ap. 6. II. 4.

my wretchedness. Should be "thy evil", evil being put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6. One of the eighteen emendations of the Sopherim. See Ap. 33. wretchedness. Heb. ra'a'. See Ap. 44. viii., put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for punishment due, see above.
said. See note on 3. 40. to be = "that [they] be". tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40.
take of = withdraw. spirit. Heb. ruach, spirit, put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the gifts and manifestations of the Holy Spirit. Cp. 1 Cor. 12. 4. See Ap. 9.
sanctify = separate. See note on "holy". Ex. 3. 5.
nor. Fig. Paradiastole, Ap. 6, for emphasis.
whole month = a month of days.
them. Some codices have a reading called Sevir (Ap. 34), which reads "unto you".
Is ...? &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. hand. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for power exercised by it.
People. Some codices, with Jon. and Vulg., read "Israel". tabernacle. Heb. 'ohel, tent. See Ap. 40.

spake. See note on 1. 1. did not cease. So the Vulg.; but Heb. = "did not add" (so Sept. and Syr.), i.e. did not add any more, or again, after that day. Cp. Ex. 11. 6. Deut. 5. 22. Job. 38. 11. 1 Sam. 19. 24.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. them = the seventy. written = enrolled. See note on Ex. 17. 14. went not out. Cp. 1 Sam. 10. 22. in the camp. Cp. Ps. 139. 7.
a. Heb. the, viz. the young man, to be described later.

Enviest thou ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. Art thou jealous for me? would God. "God" should be in italics. Fig. Oeonismos. Ap. 6. put His spirit. This is the definition of a true prophet. Cp. v. 17, and 12. 6.

wind. Heb. ruach. Ap. 9. fall. Cp. Ps. 78. 27, 28. a day's journey. See Ap. 51. III. 4. cubits. See Ap. 51. III. 2. high upon. Heb. = "above"; i.e. "[flying] above", so that they could be easily caught. It does not say "deep".
homers. See Lev. 27. 16, and Ap. 51. III. 3.
flesh. Cp. Ps. 78. 27-31.
Kibroth-hattaavah. Heb. graves of lust.

12. 1-15 (r, p. 195). MURMURINGS OF MIRIAM AND AARON (Alternation). Miriam. Named first to show she was first in the rebellion. See v. 10. Cp. Gen. 3. 3. Ethiopian = Zipporah. Heb. Cushite. Arabia was in the land of Cush: or Zipporah (Ex. 2. 21) may have been of Cushite nationality, though territorially a Midianite.
Hath ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.

man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. very meek = patient. First occurrence. Heb. 'anah = to endure with submission what might be evaded: in contrast with Heb. 'ani = to bear what cannot be avoided. men. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14.
4-10 (c, above). PUNISHMENT INFLICTED. (Alternation.) spake. See note on 1. 1. tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40.
door = entrance.
He: i.e. Jehovah. said. See note on 3. 40. If there be = should there be; i.e. when ye have your prophet. make Myself known. This also essential to a prophet. Cp. 11. 29.

My servant Moses. First occurrence. Occurs six times. See Num. 12. 7, 8. Josh. 1. 2, 7. 2 Kings 21. 8. Mal. 4. 4. not so: i.e. much greater. Cp. v. 8. who is faithful. Cp. Heb. 3. 2, or, Faithful is he, &c.

mouth to mouth. Cp. Gen. 45. 12. 2 John 12. 3 John 14. See also Ex. 33. 11. Deut. 34. 10. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. apparently = plainly. not, &c. = Fig. Pleonasm. Ap. 6. similitude: i.e. likeness or image. This must be understood in harmony with Ex. 33. 20, 23. Cp. Deut. 4. 12, 15. John 1. 18. 1 Tim. 6. 16. Cp. Col. 1. 15. against, &c. Heb. "against my servant, against Moses." Cp. idiom in Gen. 21. 10 and note.
kindled: with instant result. He: i.e. Jehovah.
leprous. See note on Ex. 4. 6. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. = "there she was—leprous!" abruptness of language reveals the excitement produced.
sin ... sinned. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i.

dead = stillborn. the flesh. The Primitive Text read "our flesh". This is one of the eighteen emendations of the Sopherim (see Ap. 33), to avoid what was supposed to be derogatory to Aaron. his mother's. The Primitive Text read "our mother's" (see above note): thus it is made impersonal.
GOD = El. = God, the mighty God. See Ap. 4. iv.

spit in her face = treat with contempt: so the idiom is used in Syr. and Arabic to-day. Heb. "had spitted a spitting." Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis. Cp. Job 30. 10. seven days. Cp. Lev. 13. 4, 5, 21, 26. received in. Homonym 'asaph (1) to heal or recover, here, 2 Kings 5. 6. Ps. 27. 10; (2) to snatch away or destroy, Ps. 26. 9. Jer. 16. 5.
brought = received, v. 14.

13. 1—14. 45 [For Structures see next page]. 13. 1—14. 45 (N2, p. 195). THE SPIES (Division). 13. 1—14. 38 (O1, above). THE EXPEDITION. (Introversion and Alternation.) the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

Send thou. This was spoken in consequence of People's request. Cp. Deut. 1. 19-22, and "we will" of v. 22. This was walking by "sight." men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. ii. search, for Jehovah had told them about it. See Deut. 8. 7-9. Cp. 1 Sam. 8. 6, 22, and Hos. 13. 11. Jehovah already espied it. Ezek. 20. 6. Canaan. Cp. Deut. 7. 1. The land of the seven mighty nations. See App. 23 and 25. children = sons. man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. = a great or chief man. Cp. Isa. 5. 15. ruler: or prince. This made the rebellion so serious.
by the commandment of the LORD. Cp. Deut. 1. 19-22. commandment. Heb. "mouth". Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, put for what is spoken by the mouth. heads = captains over thousands. Ex. 18. 25.
names. For the order of the tribes here, see Ap. 45.
Oshea = salvation. Cp. v. 16. See note on v. 16. Nun. 1 Chron. 7. 27, "Non".
Sethur = hidden, or mystical: by Gematria = 666 (Ap. 10). Probably marking the ringleader of the Provocation.

names. Levi not named. No inheritance in the land. Jehoshua. Name occurs over 250 times; see the first, Ex. 17. 9. Sometimes Jeshua (Neh. 8. 17). Greek, Jesus (Matt. 1. 21. Acts 7. 45. Heb. 4. 8). In Deut. 32. 44 called Hoshea again: Hoshea = saviour, or salvation. Je, prefixed = he by whom Jehovah will save.
southward. For first nine miles, on account of the roads, then by the mountain passes eastward.
tents = camps.
went up. In the month Ab (our July).

south = the Negeb. Cp. Gen. 12. 9; 13. 1. Hebron. Ancient name, Kirjath-arba (or stronghold of Arba) (Gen. 23. 2, 19), because built by Anak and the sons of Arba. Josh. 14. 15; 15. 13. The Tel-el-Amarna Tablets show that certain bands of Hittite condottieri are called "Khabiri", or "allies" (hence the name Hebron, which means "confederacy", or friendship, which is not met with till Ramases II), captured Kirjath-Arba. Ebed-Tob, king of Jerusalem (see note on Gen. 14. 18), in his letters to Pharaoh frequently mentions these Khabiri (or confederates of Amorites and Hittites). God's confederacy with His people in Christ was "before the foundation of the world". Before Zoan the city of the wise was known. Ahiman. Driven out by Caleb. Josh. 15. 13, 14. Slain by Judah. Judg. 1. 10. children of Anak = home-born persons: usually of slaves. These were the result of a second irruption of the fallen angels. See Gen. 6. 4, "after that". These are called "Nephilim" in v. 33. See Ap. 23 and 25. The name "Anak" occurs here, and vv. 28, 33. Deut. 9. 2. Josh. 15. 14. built: i.e. rebuilt (banah frequently has this meaning). Cp. Josh. 6. 26. 1 Kings 16. 34. 2 Kings 14. 22. Isa. 44. 28. Amos 9. 14. seven years before Zoan in Egypt. Built by the first kings of the nineteenth dynasty (see Ap. 37). Ramases II made it his capital, cp. Isa. 30. 4 (and is the first to mention Hebron). Zoan was the scene of the Exodus (see Ps. 78. 12, 13), and "the house of bondage". Zoan. See note on Ex. 1. 10.

And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), calling attention to each of the three items. grapes, &c. No mere accident that these three were brought. These symbolical of the "fruit" of our Land, even of Him Who is the true Vine. He comes first. pomegranates. His worship comes next (largely used symbolically in tabernacle and temple, see Ex. 27, 28, and 29 and 2 Chron. 3 and 4). figs. The common support of life in the East, next to bread. These symbolise the common duties of life. (The grapes and pomegranates its luxuries and spiritual privileges).
brook: or valley. Eshcol = cluster. cluster. Heb. 'eshcol.
forty. The number of Probation. See Ap. 10. At the end of Elul (our August), exactly six months from setting up of the Tabernacle. See Ap. 50. VII. 3.
13. 26—14. 10- (b, p. 198). REPORT AND RECEPTION (Introversions). Kadesh = Kadesh-barnea. Deut. 1. 19.

Nevertheless. In spite of the evidence produced. This is the conclusion of sight, not of faith. Note the words "we saw", vv. 28, 32, 33. very great. Great in size as well as in wickedness, abnormal, superhuman. See Ap. 23 and 25. we saw. This was "walking by sight, not by faith", 2 Cor. 5. 7.
Caleb = whole-hearted. stilled = silenced. well able = the conclusion of faith.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. ii. not able = the conclusion of sight. they are stronger than we = the conclusion of unbelief, which always leaves God out.
brought up an evil report = sent forth a slander. Cp. 14. 37. we saw. The language of unbelief.

giants. Heb. nephilim. Those mentioned in Gen. 6. 4 were all destroyed in the Flood; these came from a second irruption of fallen angels, "after that": i.e. after "those days" = the days of Noah. See Gen. 6. 4, and Ap. 23 and 25. See note on v. 22. sight. It is all "sight" where there is no faith 2 Cor. 5. 7. grasshoppers: or locusts.

lifted up their voice. Heb. idiom "lifted up and gave their voice". Gen. 21. 16. Ps. 18. 13. Jer. 2. 15. Ps. 104. 12; 77. 18. Hab. 3. 10. cried = cried aloud. What a contrast to Ex. 15. 1, "Then sang". Cp. Ex. 15. 13-17, and note 1 Cor. 10. 11.
children = sons. Would God. Fig. Oeonismus. Ap. 6.
wherefore. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. were it not ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
captain. At Horeb they made a "calf"; at Kadesh they would make a "captain". Two notable occasions.
Joshua ... and Caleb. Only two out of twelve; only two out of the whole congregation. Let us heed the lesson, and take courage. 1 Cor. 10. 11.
exceeding. Heb. "very, very". Fig. Epizeuxis. Ap. 6.
If the LORD delight in us. This is the secret of all blessing. Deut. 10. 15. 2 Sam. 15. 25, 26; 22. 20. 1 Kings 10. 9. Ps. 22. 8; 147. 10, 11. Isa. 62. 4.

defence. Heb. = shadow. Note Fig. Ellipsis (Ap. 6. i. 2). Lit. "they [are] like our bread (= manna), their shadow hath turned aside from off them". The manna when out of the shade melted, though hard (cp. 11. 8 and Ex. 16. 21): so the hearts of their enemies would melt away, not having Jehovah for their shadow, or defence. Cp. Ex. 15. 15. Josh. 2. 9, 11. Isa. 13. 7; 19. 1. Ezek. 21. 7.
-10-38 (P, p. 198). PROVOCATION OF JEHOVAH. (Introversion and Alternation.) tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40.
said. See note on 3. 40. How long ...? = to what point. Cp. v. 27. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
13-25 (S, above). MOSES AND JEHOVAH (Alternation.) from among. Fig. Pleonasm (Ap. 6). = "out of the midst of".
face to face. Heb. eye to eye. Thy cloud. Cp Ex. 13. 21.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
my LORD = Jehovah. One of the 134 alterations of the Sopherim. See Ap. 32. Many codices, and first printed edition, read "Jehovah".

The LORD = Jehovah. Quoted from Ex. 34. 6; 20. 5 and 34. 7. mercy = lovingkindness, or grace. iniquity. Heb. 'avah. Ap. 44. iv. transgression. Heb. pash'a. Ap. 44. ix. Some codices, with Sam., Jon., and Sept., read "transgression and sin", as in Ex. 34. 7.

as I live. Heb. "assuredly I live; and all the earth", &c. Cp. Ezek. 18. 3; 20. 33. Rom. 14. 11. all the earth. First occurrence of this expression. Cp. Isa. 6. 3; 11. 9. Ps. 72. 19. Hab. 2. 14. Note the unconditional covenant.

men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. ten times. Not a "round" number:— (1) At Red Sea (Ex. 14. 11, 12). (2) At Marah (Ex. 15. 23, 24). (3) Wilderness of Sin (Ex. 16. 2). (4, 5) Twice about manna (Ex. 16. 20, 27). (6) At Rephidim (Ex. 17. 1-3). (7) At Horeb (golden calf) (Ex. 32). (8) At Taberah (Num. 11. 1). (9) At Kibroth Hattaavah (Num. 11. 4). (10) Here, at Kadesh (Num. 14. 2).
another = different. Cp. Phil. 3. 15, "otherwise". Cp. Eph. 4. 23. spirit. Heb. ruach. Spirit put for motions of the mind and character (Ap. 9).
How long ...? = to what time. Cp. v. 11. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. shall I bear with. Fig. Ellipsis. Ap. 6. ii. 2.
28-38 (g, above). THREATENING. (Alternations.) as = according as ... so will I do. Ps. 95. 11. Num. 26. 65; 32. 11. Deut. 1. 35. Heb. 3. 17, 18.
numbered. Cp. 1. 45 and 26. 63-65.
I sware. Heb. I lifted up my hand. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, put for swearing. Cp. v. 21. Deut. 32. 40, &c.
ye said. v. 3. Cp. Deut. 1. 39. know = get to know, and enjoy. Sept. = shall inherit.
wander = be wanderers. whoredoms. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the punishment they produced, all caused by idolatry. Cp. Jer. 3. 9. Ezek. 16. 15-17. Ex. 34. 15, 16. Lev. 17. 7.

forty days. See Ap. 10. The number of Probation. See also Ap. 50. VII. 2. each day for a year. No universal law here: "day" means day, and "year" means year. See Ap. 11. breach = "my breach of promise (cp. vv. 42 and 43) [with which ye charge me] meaneth". Cp. Deut. 31. 16, 17. Zech. 11. 10. Rom. 11. 22; also Job 33. 10.

said. See note on 3. 40. Said on 26 Ab (fifth month, second year). The whole period is contained in chs. 15—19; 33. 19-36, inclusive. See Ap. 50. VII. 3. shall die. Aaron died on first day of fifth month of fortieth year, 20. 28; 33. 38. The second numbering took place after that.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. These ten men died by a special plague at the time. Cp. 1 Chron. 13. 10. 2 Sam 6. 7. Cp. v. 37 here.

Lo. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. sinned. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i.

15. 1-41 (M1, p. 195). LAWS FOR THE PEOPLE. (Introversion.) 1-29 (r, above). LAWS RE OFFERINGS. (Extended Alternation, and Introversion.) the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

offering. Heb. 'ishsheh. Ap. 43. II. xi. burnt offering. Heb. 'olah. Ap. 43. II. ii. sacrifice. Heb. zebach. Ap. 43. II. xii. freewill offering. Heb. nedabah. Ap. 43. II. vii. solemn feasts = appointed seasons. sweet savour. See note on Lev. 1. 9.

sacrifice. Probably peace-offerings. Ap. 43. II. xii.
meat offering. Ap. 43. II. iii.

manner. Heb. judgment, or ordinance.

generations. Severus Codex reads this as singular. See Ap. 34.

sinneth. Heb. shagag. Ap. 44. xii.
sinneth. Heb. 'asah. Ap. 44. ii.
presumptuously. Heb. with a high hand.
