declared. Heb. parash, make known. This is the meaning of Gr. sunkrino, rendered "comparing" in 1 Cor. 2. 13. what should be done to him: i.e. what death he should die. It had been made known that he was to die, but not in what manner. Ex. 31. 15; 35. 2.
35, 36 (y2, above). THE PUNISHMENT. (Introversion.) said. See note on 3. 40.
as = according as.
fringes. Heb. zizith, a fringe, as in Deut. 22. 12. Occurs only four times: here, vv. 38, 39, and Ezek. 8. 3 (lock [of hair]) = a fringe where the threads hang down, like a lock of hair.
holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. i.
the LORD your God. Fig. Epanadiplosis. Ap. 6. The word "Jehovah" beginning and ending the verse, to emphasise it.

16. 1—17. 13 (L2, p. 195). EVENTS: REBELLION OF KORAH (Extended Alternation). 1-19- (f, above). THE SIN OF KORAH. (Introversion and Extended Alternation.) Now. See note on "while", 15. 32. Korah. First cousin to Moses and Aaron. 6. 8. 1 Chron. 6. 2, 3. These three associated, because encamped together on south side. Cp. 2. 10 and 3. 29. See p. 181. sons. Some codices, with Sam. and Sept., read "son". men. This word necessitated through A.V. and R.V. misplacing the verb "took", which should be after Levi. "Korah took Dathan ... and Abiram ... and On, the son of Peleth, the son of Reuben". See below.
children = sons. assembly = appointed assembly. congregation = assembly. Heb. 'edah. men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14.
congregation = appointed assembly. Heb. 'edah. holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. congregation = assembly.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14.
Seemeth it ...? Fig. Erotesis Ap. 6. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. tabernacle = Heb. mishkan, habitation. Ap. 40.
and what is Aaron? = "and Aaron, who is he"? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
Is it ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
put out = bore out.
offering = gift offering. Ap. 43. II. iii.
fire. Note three kinds of fire here, v. 18 strange fire; v. 35, judicial fire; v. 46, sacrificial fire. Cp. Lev. 9. 24 and 10. 1, 2. door = entrance. tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40.
20-35 (h, p. 203). PUNISHMENT. (Introversion.) spake. See note on 1. 1.
O GOD = O 'El. Ap. 4. IV. God = Elohim. Ap. 4. I. spirits. Heb. pl. of ruach. Ap. 9. man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. sin. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i.
tabernacle. Heb. mishkan, habitation in sing. here = the habitation of each, separately; in v. 26 plural, "tents".
wicked. Heb. rash'a. Ap. 44. x. men. Heb pl of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14.
they = and Korah and his sons among them. Cp. 26. 11. door = entrance. their sons: i.e. the sons of Dathan and Abiram, not of Korah. Cp. ch. 26. 11. Ps. 106. 17. See note on v. 32.
I have not done them. Fig. Ellipsis. Ap. 6. i. 4.
men. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. i.

make a new thing. Heb. "create a creation". Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6, for emphasis, throwing light on Gen. 1. 1. Cp. Isa. 45. 7; 48. 6, 7. them: Dathan and Abiram. Cp. v. 27. Korah's sons had obeyed the command, cp. 26. 11. quick = alive. pit = Sheol, see v. 33 and Ap. 35.
men: Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. These did not include Korah's sons. Cp. 26. 11.
pit = Heb. sheol = the grave, not "a" grave, but all graves viewed as one. See Ap. 35. They went alive, with all their cattle, tents, and goods. All sank into the earth.
two hundred and fifty. Plus the 14,700 of v. 49 men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. ii.
spake. See note on 1. 1.
burning. Heb. saraph. See Ap. 43. I. viii, i.e from among those that were burnt. the fire. Cp. v. 7, not accepted by Jehovah. hallowed = set apart. See note on "holy". Ex. 3. 5.
sinners. See Ap. 44. i. souls = their own selves. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. their own. Cp. Gen. 19. 17 and Prov. 20. 2. offered. Heb. brought near. Ap. 43. I. i.

memorial. Cp. ch. 17. 10, 1 Cor. 10. 11, and see Structure, p 203. Hence history rehearsed in Deut. 11. 6-8. Note the two memorials added to the tabernacle through Korah's rebellion (see the Structure, p. 203), the plates (i, 36-40) and Aaron's rod (i, 17. 1-13). offer = burn. Heb. katar. Ap. 43. I. vii. as = according as. to him, or with regard thereto.
tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33. from = from before.
the = Heb. between the.
fourteen thousand and seven hundred. This, with the 250 of v. 35 = 14,950 (= 13 x 1,150). See Ap. 10 for significance of the number 13.
door = entrance.
17. 1-13 (i, p. 203). MEMORIAL (THE RODS). (Alternations.) the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.
children = sons. man's. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40. testimony = the ark of the covenant. Cp. Ex. 25. 16 you. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., and Vulg., read "thee".

laid up the rods. Korah's rebellion added two things to the tabernacle: Aaron's rod within, brazen plates without (16. 39, 40). tabernacle of witness = tent of (or containing) the testimony (i.e. the ark, and the two tables). Ap. 40. See note on Ex. 25. 22.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.

said. See note on 3. 40. testimony = the ark of the covenant, as in v. 4. rebels. Heb. sons of rebellion. Genitive of character = rebellious ones. Ap. 17. take away = assuage, or, abate, as in v. 5. Cp. Gen. 8. 1.
we perish, we all perish. Fig. Epizeuxis (Ap. 6), to enhance the alarm of the People.
tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. Ap. 40. die ... dying. Fig. Epizeuxis (Ap. 6), as in v. 12, to emphasise alarm.

18. 1—19. 22 (M2, p. 195). LAWS FOR PRIESTS AND PEOPLE (Division). 18. 1-32 (T1, above). LAWS FOR PRIESTS AND LEVITES (Division). 1-7 (U1, above). PRIESTS AND THEIR OFFICES. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. said. See note on 3. 40. Aaron. Jehovah "spoke" again to Aaron in vv. 8 and 20. iniquity. Heb. 'avah. Ap. 44. iv.
tribe = matteh = staff. Levi ... joined. Fig. Paronomasia. Ap. 6. Heb. Levi ... v'yillavu. tribe = shebet = rod. tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40.
children = sons.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. do the service. Heb. serve the service. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6, i.e. perform the solemn service.
spake. See note on 1. 1. hallowed = holy. See note on "holy", Ex. 3. 5. the anointing. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, for the priesthood associated with it.
holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5. oblation. Heb. approach-offering. See Ap. 43. II. i. shall be. Heb. "it [shall be]".
wine. Heb. tirosh. See Ap. 27. ii.
the = their.
Every thing. See Lev. 27. 28. devoted. See note on Lev. 27. 1.
the matrix. See 3. 13. Ex. 13. 2; 34. 19. Lev. 27. 26. men ... man = Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. I. redeem. Heb. padah. See note on Ex. 6. 6.
shekels ... shekel. See Ap. 51. II. which = it. Cp. 3. 47. Ex. 30. 13. Lev. 27. 25. gerahs. See Ap. 51. III. 3.
thou. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Jon., Onk., and Syr., read "but thou". burn = burn as incense. See Ap. 43. I. vii. sweet savour. See note on Lev. 1. 9.

offer = heave up as a heave offering. See note on Ex. 29. 27. covenant of salt. Heb. covenant = b'rith, from barah, to cut; hence, to eat. As salt was scarce and precious, and used with all eating, so it was put, by Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, for eating, just as the breaking of bread was. See Isa. 58. 7 (A.V. "deal"); Jer. 16. 7 (A.V. "tear"). Lam. 4. 4. Ezek. 18. 7 (A.V. "given"). Hence, when wages were paid in kind, by finding the worker in food, "salt" was put (by Fig. Metonymy) for wages generally; so that a worker was spoken of as being worth, or not worth, his "salt". "A covenant of salt" was therefore a covenant made by sacrifice, which was first cut in two (Gen. 15. 10-18. Jer. 34. 18, 19) and then eaten, thus solemnising an inviolable covenant.
20-32 (U3, p. 206). PRIESTS AND THEIR INHERITANCE (Introversion).
for = instead of.
sin. Heb. chatah. Ap. 44. i.
of = from.
19. 1-22 (T2, p. 206). LAWS FOR THE PEOPLE. (Water of separation: The red heifer.) (Alternation.) the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

ordinance = statute. The whole clause = Fig. Pleonasm (Ap. 6), for emphasising the lesson of the red heifer. children = sons. bring = take. This is the third of three events recorded during the punishment wanderings. See note on "while", 15. 32. a red heifer. Christ, the Antitype. without spot = without defect. Cp. the Antitype. Heb. 9. 14. no blemish. Cp. 1 Pet. 1. 19.
without the camp. Cp. the Antitype. Heb. 13. 12.
tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40.
burn. Heb. saraph. See Ap. 43. I. viii.
in water. Some codices, with Sept., Syr., and Vulg., omit these words. Cp. Lev. 16. 28.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. Cp. the antitype, Joseph of Arimathea. Matt. 27. 57-60. Luke 23. 50-53. John 19. 38-42. sin. See Ap. 44. i.
11-20 (V, above). USE OF THE WATER. (Alternation.) body = soul. Heb. nephesh. Lit. "the dead nephesh of". Ap. 13. man = Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. i.
third ... seventh. Cp. the Antitype. Heb. 9. 14. The numbers significant. See Ap. 10. the = on the.
body = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. See Ap. 40. soul. Heb. nephesh (Ap. 13). Cp. vv. 11 and 13.
is = "it [is]".
dead body. Heb. b'meth, no word for body = one dead, as in v. 18, not vv. 11 and 13.
ashes = dust. sin. See Ap. 44. i. running = living. Not stagnant.
person = Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. persons = souls. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13.
wash. The common rite. See Lev. 11. 25; 14. 8, 9, &c. himself = his flesh, as in Lev. 15. 16.
soul = person. Heb. nephesh. Used of "living souls" and "dead souls". Cp. vv. 11, 13 (where it is rendered "any", and "body" respectively). See Ap. 13.

20. 1—25. 18 (L3, p. 180). EVENTS: JOURNEYINGS AND MURMURINGS. (Repeated and Extended Alternations.) -1-13 (d1, above). EVENTS: MIRIAM'S DEATH, &c. (Introversion.) Then came. This was in the first month of the fortieth year after Exodus. Cp. 20. 28 with 33. 38 and Deut. 2. 1-7. A gap of 37 1/2 years between the spies (13, 14) and this chapter. This blank should be carefully noted. See note on 14. 34, and Ap. 50. vii. 3. children = sons. and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton throughout this chapter. The old nation dead. History of new nation begins here, and each event singled out and emphasised. Kadesh. The second time in eventful Kadesh. No history since the first time—all a blank, except a list of journeyings in ch. 33. Miriam: died early in fortieth year; Aaron in the fifth month. Cp. vv. 23-29 with vv. 33, 38.
Would God. Fig. Oeonismos (Ap. 6). No Heb. for "God" here. when. Cp. 11. 33. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
why have ye ...? Sept. reads, "why hast thou?" Fig. Erotesis (Ap. 6). congregation = assembly.

wherefore ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. evil. See Ap. 44. viii. or of. Note Fig. Paradiastole, Ap. 6, to emphasise the three items: figs, vines, and pomegranates. figs, vines, ... pomegranates. See note on 13. 23.
door = entrance. tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40.
spake. See note on 1. 1.
the rod. Cp. 17. 5. Some think (from v. 9) the rod "from before the testimony", as in 17. 10; but v. 11 it is "his rod". assembly = congregation. speak ye unto the rock. Not "smite" as in v. 11.
as = according as.
said. He spoke to the People instead of to the rock. must we ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
his: i.e. Moses' tribal rod. Cp. v. 8. smote. Instead of speaking. twice. Showing the heat of his feeling. drank. Cp. 1 Cor. 10. 4, and see note there.

believed Me not. So Moses entered not in, because of unbelief. Me. Hence called "rebellion" in v. 24 and 27. 14. Cp. Deut. 32. 51. Cp. "we" in v. 10. in the eyes, &c. His complaint in 11. 21-23 was not public.
Meribah = contention. Ps. 106. 32, &c. He was sanctified = He hallowed Himself. See note on "holy", Ex. 3. 5. Cp. Ezek. 38. 23.
20. 14-21 (e1, p. 209). OPPOSITION OF EDOM. (Alternation.) befallen us = "found us". Fig. Prosopopoeia. Ap. 6.
behold. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6), to emphasise the importance of the place. See notes on v. 1.
wells. Heb. b'er. See note on Gen. 21. 19.
by me = through me. "Me" put by Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, for "my country".
without doing any thing else. Heb. "without a word": i.e. without [saying] a word. Fig. Ellipsis. Ap. 6.
turned away. Cp. Judg. 11. 18. Deut. 2. 4, 5.
Kadesh. See notes on v. 1, and cp. 33. 37. Hor. Cp. 33. 37.
23-26 (d2, p. 209). EVENT: THE DEATH OF AARON (Alternation).

gathered. Fig. Euphemismos (Ap. 6) for dying = die, and be buried as all his fathers were, Sheol being the grave. See Ap. 35. Cp. Gen. 25. 8. Ps. 26. 9. Acts 13. 36. word. Heb. "mouth". Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for what was spoken by it. Cp. v. 12.
unto his people. Fig. Ellipsis, supplied from v. 24. See Ap. 6. iii. 1.
as = according as.
top of the mount. Cp. Gen. 8. 4; 22. 2. Ex. 19. Matt. 5. 1. Ezek. 40. 2. Rev. 21. 10. Deut. 34. 1-5. Matt. 17. 1-3.

saw. Heb. ra'ah, to perceive, understand. Cp. Gen. 16. 13; 42. 1. Ex. 20. 18. dead. The death of Aaron coincides with the end of the wanderings. the house of Israel. See note on Ex. 16. 31; one of the thirteen occurrences of the expression before the division of the two kingdoms; and cp. note on 1 Kings 12. 17.

21. 1-3 (e2, p. 209). OPPOSITION OF ARAD. (Introversion.) Arad. Cp. Josh. 12. 14. south = the Negeb. See Gen. 12. 9; 13. 1, 3; 24. 62. Num. 13. 17. came = was entering. way of the spies. 13. 21, &c. = "the way of the Atharim". Sept. so renders it, as a proper name; probably the name of the caravan route.

vowed a vow. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis = made a solemn vow. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. wilt indeed deliver = same Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), only here it is translated and emphatically expressed by the word "indeed". Heb. = "a delivering Thou wilt deliver".
Canaanites. The Sept. and Sam. add "into his (i.e. Israel's) hand". and their cities. These destroyed after Israel came into the land. Cp. Josh. 12. 14. Judg. 1. 16, 17. Hormah = utter destruction.
soul. Heb. nephesh (Ap. 13). discouraged = grieved or impatient.
God = Elohim. They had lost sight of the covenant God, Jehovah. Cp. Ap. 4. I. II. Wherefore ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. our soul = we. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13.

6-9 (e3, p. 209). THE FIERY SERPENTS. fiery serpents = burning. Heb. nacheshim saraphim. Fig. Metonymy (of Effect), Ap. 6, because the effect of the bite was a burning sensation. Heb. saraph (see Ap. 43. I. viii). The Seraphim so called in Isa. 6. 2, because they were burning ones: hence the name for these serpents. In the same way nachash, shining one, is also used for serpents, because they are shining ones in appearance. See Gen. 3. 1, and cp. Ap. 19.
sinned. See Ap. 44. i.
said. See note on 3. 40.

serpent = Heb. nachash, a shining thing of brass, as in Deut. 8. 15. 2 Kings 18. 4, &c.: so that nachash is synonymous with saraph, and both words are thus used of serpents. he lived. Cp. John 3. 14, 15.
children = sons.
coasts = border.

of the wars of the LORD. This may commence the quotation, thus: "the wars of Jehovah [were with] Eth-Vaheb by the Red sea (or with a whirlwind. Heb. Supha. Cp. Amos 1. 14. Isa. 66. 15. Nah 1. 3. Jer. 4. 13) and by the brooks of Arnon". Eth-Vaheb may be the proper name of the king of the Amorites, who took Heshbon, as in v. 26. the Red sea. Heb. Suphah, a city situated as described here, and in Deut. 1. 1. Cp. 1 Kings 9. 26. the brooks of Arnon = the outpouring of the torrents.
they went. This Ellipsis is wrongly supplied. It should be "from thence toward Beer". No mention is made of Beer in the list of journeys in ch. 33. spake. See note on 1. 1.
this song. See note on Ex. 15. 1.

they went. No mention is made of any of these places in the itinerary in ch. 33. Why not supply "[the waters or streams] went" into all these places? See v. 16. The Structure shows the scope of this member to be an "event"; "journeys" are the subject of the preceding member. Cp. note on Ex. 15. 27. Note the Alternation, which gives the interpretation: The princes digged the well; The nobles of the people digged it, With the lawgiver [They digged it] with their staves.
country = field. Jeshimon = the wilderness.
21-31 (e4, p. 209). OPPOSITION OF SIHON. (Alternation.)
would not suffer. Fig. Tapeinosis, Ap. 6, much more being meant, even armed opposition.
25-31 (s, above). POSSESSION. (Introversion.) villages = Heb. daughters. Fig. Prosopopoeia Ap. 6.
27-30 (u, above). SAYINGS. (Introversion.) proverbs. Heb. poems.
the lords. Heb. Baalim. high places. Cp. 22. 41 and Jer. 48. 35.

We = Israel. we have laid, &c., to end of verse. These two clauses are affected by the "extraordinary points" (see Ap 31), which necessitates the following rendering of v. 30:— "We have shot them down: Heshbon is destroyed even unto Dibon, The women also even unto Nopha, And the men even unto Medeba."
thou shalt do, &c. Cp. Ps. 135. 11.
children = sons. plains of Moab: i.e. which had belonged to Moab.
done to the Amorites. Cp. 21. 35.
all that are round about us: Heb. all our circuits. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject). Ap. 6.

22. 5—25. 18 [For Structures see next page]. 22. 5—25. 18 (e6, p. 209). OPPOSITION OF BALAK (Repeated Alternation). These five members are each expanded below. 22. 5-20 (v1, above). BALAK'S MESSAGES TO BALAAM (Extended Alternation). Balaam. So written after the Greek. In Heb. his name is Bil'am. Cp. Josh. 13. 22 and 24. 9, 10. 2 Pet. 2. 15, 16. He was a spiritist or medium. He is identified by Sayce with Bela, Gen. 36. 31, 32, where Moses incorporates a list of Edomite kings. According to the Tel-el-Amarna tablets he was a Hittite chieftain, who established a kingdom for himself: and he died fighting against Israel by the side of his Midianite allies (31. 8. Jos. 13. 22). Beor. Heb. = B'e'or. In 1 Pet. 2. 15 called Bosor. The Heb. letter (ayin = 'o), often pronounced "s" by Greeks. Pethor. A city in Aram (23. 7) or Mesopotamia (Deut. 23. 4). his people: i.e. whom he had banded together and led. Some codices, with Sam., Syr., and Vulg., read "sons of Ammon". Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. behold. For this second word some codices, with Sam., Onk., Jon., Sept., and Syr., read "and behold". face. Heb "eye". Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6; also Fig. Prosopopoeia. Ap. 6. abide = sit, i.e. ready for war, having subdued the Amorites, ch. 21, cp. Job 38. 40. Ps. 10. 8; 17. 12.
curse. Heb. 'arar. To wish or speak evil against, as to effect rather than as to the act. wot = know.
rewards of divination. Heb. "divinations". Fig. Metonymy (of Effect), Ap. 6, put for the money which procures it. Cp. 2 Pet. 2. 15.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. II.
God ... said. Note the change to 'Elohim. said. Only four times: in vv. 9, 12, 20: in connection with Balaam. See Ap. 4, and notes on 1. 1; 3. 40.

there is a People. Heb. = the People. now. Some codices, with Sam., Jon., and Sept., read "now therefore". curse. Heb. kabab, to pierce with words. Note that this word is found only in Balak's and Balaam's mouths. Here, first occurrence, and later in seven other places. See note on 23. 8. peradventure = perhaps.

not go. This is absolute. Cp. v. 20, where the permission is conditional. See Structure above. thou shalt not curse. A special various reading called Sevir (see Ap. 34), with Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "neither shalt thou".
Balaam ... said. Note what he suppressed.
they ... said. Note what they suppressed.
promote thee unto very great honour. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for the emphasis rightly shown in the translation. Heb. an honouring I will honour thee. See note on Gen. 26. 28.
If the men come to call thee. This was the condition with which Balaam did not comply. See v. 21.
22. 21-35 (w1, above). BALAAM'S JOURNEY. (Introversion, with Repeated and Extended Alternation.) went. Without waiting for the condition given by the LORD in v. 20. Hence God's anger. See v. 22.

God's anger. Note 'Elohim, not Jehovah. went = was really going. Emphasised to show that even this condition was not meant as a condition, but was to be taken rather as irony. It shows also Balaam's determination to go, whether or no. stood = stationed himself.
His sword drawn. As in 1 Chron. 21. 16. Balaam was going to have Israel killed with the sword.
path = a narrow or hollow way. Heb. mish'ol. Occurs only here. wall. Especially the wall of a vineyard. Cp. Isa. 5. 5.
narrow. Heb. zarar. Occurs only here, Prov. 23. 27, and Isa. 28. 20.

28-35- (c, p. 213). THE REBUKE OF JEHOVAH. (Alternation and Introversion.) opened the mouth, &c. Heb. patah. Cp. v. 31. This was Jehovah's work (as in v. 31). But how could Satan open the mouth of the serpent, which has no organs of speech? See Gen. 3. 1, &c., and Ap. 19.
opened = uncover. Heb. galah. Cp. v. 28.

said. See note on 3. 40. Wherefore ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. to withstand = to be an adversary, as in v. 22. perverse. Heb. 'avil. Occurs only here and Job 16. 11 (ungodly).
thee ... her. Note the emphasis on these pronouns.
sinned. Heb. chata. Ap. 44. i.
Go. Jehovah now overrules the evil for Israel's good. men = Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14. II. only the word. Permission limited.
36-40 (v2, p. 213). BALAK'S RECEPTION OF BALAAM (First Day). coast = border.
Did I not earnestly send. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), Heb. "a sending did I not send". See note on Gen. 26. 28. am I not able ...? Vain boast! Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
Lo. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6). have I ...? Fig. Erotesis (Ap. 6). God = 'Elohim. Not Jehovah. Note this, and see Ap. 4.
offered. Heb. zabach, to slay. See Ap. 43. I. iv.
22. 41—24. 25 (w2, p. 213). BALAAM'S PROPHECIES (Second Day): (Division). 22. 41—23. 26 (t1, above). WITH ENCHANTMENTS (Extended Alternation). the utmost part = the extremity of the camp.
as = according to what. offered = offered up. Heb. 'alah. See Ap. 43. I. vi.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. See Ap. 4. II. meet: in a neutral sense. Heb. kar'a. he went. Heb. he went solitary. Cp. 24. 1.
God. Heb. 'Elohim. See Ap. 4. I. met: in a hostile sense. Heb. karah.
put a word. This is inspiration. said. See note on 3. 40.
lo. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6).
7-10 (z, above). BALAAM'S FIRST PARABLE. (Introversion.) curse. Heb. 'arar. See notes on 22. 6 and 11.
How ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. curse = revile. Heb. nakab. GOD = Heb. 'El = the mighty God. See Ap. 4. IV. cursed. Heb. kabab = to pierce with words. defy ... defied. Heb. za'am = to be enraged with.
not be reckoned. Therefore cannot be in the judgment of Matt. 25, or confused with "the Gentiles, or with the church of God". 1 Cor. 10. 32.

Who can count ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. the number of = Who can number? Fig. Erotesis (Ap. 6). So with Sam. and Sept. The word "number" is thought by Ginsburg to be an abbreviation of two words = "Who can number?" me die = my soul die. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13. righteous = upright. To die the death of the righteous one must have the righteousness of the righteous. last end = latter end, i.e. issue or reward.
curse. Heb. kabab. See note on 22. 11.
burnt offering. Some codices, one early printed edition, with Sam. and Syr., read "offerings" (plural).
behold. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6).
18-24 (z, p. 215). BALAAM'S SECOND PARABLE. (Division.) 18-20 (e1, above). GOD'S IMMUTABLE PURPOSE. (Division.)
Hath He said. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
He hath blessed. Sam. and Sept. read "I will bless".
21-24 (e2, above). ISRAEL'S IMMUTABLE PRIVILEGES (Extended Alternation). iniquity. Heb. 'avon, trespass. Ap. 44. III. perverseness. Heb. 'amal. Ap. 44. v.

strength = heights or heaps of. Heb. to'apoth. Only here, 24. 8, Job 22. 25 (plenty), and Ps. 95. 4 (= heights). unicorn. This word is from the Sept. The Heb. is r'em. Supposed to be the rhinoceros, buffalo, or antelope: always rendered "unicorn" in A.V.
23. 27—24. 25 (t2, p. 215). WITHOUT ENCHANTMENTS. (Extended Alternation. Corresponding with t1, p. 215.)
Jeshimon. See note on 21. 20.
offered = offered up. Heb. 'alah. Ap. 43. II. ii.

pleased the LORD. Heb. was good in the eyes of Jehovah. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. other times. Cp. 23. 3, 15, and see Structure (t1, p. 215). to seek for enchantments = to meet with familiar spirits (Deut. 18. 10, 14). Heb. n'chashim, from nachash, a serpent. Cp. Gen. 3. 1, and see Ap. 19.

according to their tribes. Cp. ch. 2. the spirit of God (Heb. 'Elohim). This expression occurs eight times outside the books of Samuel (Gen. 1. 2; 41. 38. Ex. 31. 3; 35. 31. Num. 24. 2. Ezek. 11. 24. 2 Chron. 15. 1; 24. 20). In all other places it is "the spirit of Jehovah". Spirit. Heb. ruach. Ap. 9. upon. Always "upon" (not "in") in Old Testament.

3-25 (p, above). BALAAM'S THIRD AND FOURTH PARABLES (Alternation and Introversion). 3-9 [For Structure see next page]. And he took up his parable. Cp. 23. 7, 18. the man = the strong or mighty man. Heb. geber. See Ap. 14. IV. whose eyes are. Heb. "whose eye is". open. Heb. shatham, to close, i.e. "the man with closed eye", i.e. in an ecstasy; closed, but seeing.

of. Genitive of origin = words from God. GOD = the mighty God. Heb. 'El. Ap. 4. iv. 3-9 ("q", p. 216). BALAAM'S THIRD PARABLE. (Repeated Alternation.) the ALMIGHTY = Shaddai, the All-bountiful or All-sufficient. See Ap. 4. VII. falling into a trance. The Ellipsis better supplied = "falling [to the ground]".

How goodly. Fig. Thaumasmos. Ap. 6. This is only in "the vision of the Almighty". Jacob. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), put for posterity (Ap. 6). And. This not to be in italics, according to some codices, with Sam., Jon., Syr., and Vulg. Israel. See note on "Jacob", v. 5.
As the trees of lign aloes, &c. Some codices, with Jon., Sept., and Syr., read "as tents which Jehovah hath pitched".
pour the water. This refers to Millennial blessings. See Ezek. 47 and Zech. 14.
him. Some codices, with Onk., Jon., and Syr., read "them". Cp. 23. 22. unicorn. See note on 23. 22.
He couched, &c. Cp. Gen. 49. 9. cursed ... curseth. Heb. 'arar, execrate, chiefly as to its effect. See notes on 22. 11; 23. 8.

Balak's anger. See note on Ex. 10. 28. curse = to pierce with words. Heb. kabab. See note on 22. 11. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. altogether blessed. Heb. "a blessing thou hast blessed". Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. See note on Gen. 26. 28.
promote thee unto great honour. See note on 22. 17, 37. lo. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
the latter days = the end of the days, denoting a definite period. Cp. Gen. 49. 1. Deut. 4. 30. Isa. 2. 2. Jer. 23. 20; 30. 24; 48. 47; 49. 39. Ezek. 38. 16. Dan. 10. 14. Hos. 3. 5. Mic. 4. 1.
15-24 ("q", p. 216). BALAAM'S FOURTH PARABLE (Division).
Most High. Heb. Elyon, the High One over all the earth. See note on first occurrence, Gen. 14. 18. The Old Testament usage of this title is always in connection with dominion in the earth. Ap. 4.

17-19 (w1, above). ISRAEL. (Introversion.) but not. Heb. Who is not. Star. Heb. kokab = Messiah. See Luke 1. 78. 2 Pet. 1. 19. Rev. 2. 28; 22. 16, and cp. Matt. 2. 2. Sceptre. See note on Gen. 49. 10, and cp. Ps. 2. corners = quarters. destroy = subdue. Sheth = Seth, i.e. all men, for all are now descendants of Sheth through Noah.
Out of Jacob. In Heb. there is the Ellipsis of the Participle (Ap. 6); "shall come" is implied and should be repeated from the previous clause. R.V. is literal.
the first: i.e. the first that warred against Israel. Ex. 17. 8. Not the first in time or importance. shall be, &c. = "[shall be] destruction". Cp. Ex. 17. 16.
Kenites. With the word "nest" forms the Fig. Paronomasia (Ap. 6). Heb. ben kain. nest. Heb. ken.
took up. This is not a fifth parable, but part of the fourth. live = survive.

Chittim. A son of Javan, son of Japheth. Gen. 10. 4. Probably Cyprus, including north coast-line of Mediterranean, spelt Kittim in Gen. 10. 4 and 1 Chron. 1. 7. afflict = humble. Asshur = Assyrians. Eber = the Hebrews. he also: i.e. who sends the ships and humbled Asshur and Heber.

25. 1-18 (v3, p. 213). BALAK'S TEACHING BY BALAAM (Cp. 31. 16 with Rev. 2. 14). (Division.) 1-9 (z1, above). BALAK'S TEACHING AND ITS RESULTS (Alternation). abode: i.e. till after Moses' death. Cp. Josh. 2. 1; 3. 1, and see Mic. 6. 5. Shittim. Called Abel-shittim in 33. 49. with = to (Heb. 'el). Requiring the supply of the Ellipsis "to join themselves to", from v. 3.
they: i.e. the daughters of Moab. their. Feminine pronoun.

joined = yoked. Baal-peor. Baal = Lord; Peor was the mountain on which he was worshipped (25. 18. Josh. 22. 17). Baal was a Moabitish idol, and those who called (v. 2) the Israelites were the prostitutes necessary for his worship by others. Cp. Hos. 9. 10. Jer. 11. 13. Peor also means "opening", and may have relation to this "worship". anger of the LORD (Heb. Jehovah). Cp. Ps. 106. 28, 29.

said. See note on 3. 40. heads: i.e. chiefs or princes of the People. The number not stated here, but must have been 1,000, and included in the 24,000 of v. 9, and excluded in 1 Cor. 10. 8. The 23,000 mentioned in 1 Cor. 10. 8 "fell in one day": the day of the plague, vv. 9, 18. And those who were hanged prior to that (vv. 4, 5) are not included. hang them up: i.e. impaled or nailed to a stake, as in crucifixion (Vulg. renders it "crucify", which means the same thing).
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. children = sons. who = and they. door = entrance. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40. tabernacle = tent.
Phinehas. Cp. Ps. 106. 30.

man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. tent. Heb. kubbah, a high and vaulted pleasure tent, used in the worship of Baal. Occurs only here. belly. Heb. kobah, the part between the ribs and loins. Occurs only here, for the Fig. Paronomasia (Ap. 6).
twenty and four thousand. This includes the 1,000 previously "hanged" (vv. 4, 5), as well as those who died of the "plague". These must have been 23,000 of 1 Cor. 10. 8, which "fell in one day".
10-18 (z2, above). JEHOVAH'S ACTION AND ITS RESULTS (Division). spake. See note on 1. 1.

he shall have it. See Ps. 106. 30, 31 and Mal. 2. 4, 5. Cp. 1 Chron. 6. 4-15. 1 Sam. 22. 18. 1 Kings 2. 27 with 1 Sam. 14. 17. Also 1 Chron. 6. 4-15. Ezra was of his line (Ezra 7. 1, 5). everlasting priesthood. Restored to Phinehas, and remained with him, after Eli. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33.
people = clan or tribe. Heb. 'ummoth. Occurs only here, Gen. 25. 16 and Ps. 117. 1.
Vex. Cp. ch. 31.
wiles = seductions. Heb. nekal. Occurs only here. day: i.e. the "one day" of 1 Cor. 10. 8.

26. 1—27. 11 (A3, p. 176). NUMERATION AND ORDER: INHERITANCE (Alternation). 1-51 (A, above). THE PEOPLE. (Introversion and Division.) after the plague. Cp. 25. 9. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

Take the sum. For the order of the tribes see Ap. 45. Moses received them by number, Ex. 38. 26; so now, when preparing to die, he delivers them over by number. This was the third numbering. children = sons. their fathers' house: i.e. the families. These shown here to be forty-seven. In Gen. 46 they are fifty-two; so five are extinct (one of Simeon, one of Asher, and three of Benjamin).
Take the sum of the people. This correctly supplies the Ellipsis from v. 2. See Fig. Ellipsis, Ap. 6. iii. 1. as = according to what.
Reuben. Cp. Gen. 46. 8. Ex. 6. 14. The order is the same as in 1. 20, except that Ephraim and Manasseh are reversed. See Ap. 45. family. See note on "house", v. 2, and throughout the chapter.
Of Hezron = To Hezron [pertained], and so throughout. Cp. vv. 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 20, 21, 23, 24, 26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32.
forty and three, &c. = 43,730 In Num. 1. 21 = 46,500, decrease of 2,770. This is an undesigned evidence of accuracy: an uninspired writer would have made an increase.
sons. A special reading of MS. called Sevir reads "son". See Ap. 34.
which were famous, &c. Heb. "the called of the congregation". No Ellipsis. strove = struggled. Heb. nazah. Cp. Ex. 2. 13. Lev. 24. 10. 2 Sam. 14. 6. Cp. 16. 2, 3.
And the earth. This tenth verse is a Parenthesis. See Ap. 6. sign: i.e. a warning.

the children of Korah died not. Cp. 16. 32, 35. They were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph (Ex. 6. 24). Their descendants were prominent in the Temple-worship (1 Chron. 6. 22-38). Of them came Samuel (cp. 1 Chron. 6. 33, 4 with 1 Sam. 1. 20) and Heman (cp. 1 Chron. 6. 33 with 25. 4, 6). Two groups of Psalms are associated with them (42-49 and 84-88).
twenty and two, &c. In Num. 1. 23 = 59,300, decrease 37,100.
forty thousand, &c. = 40,500. In Num. 2. 15 = 45,650, decrease 5,150.
threescore, &c. = 76,500. In Num. 2. 4 = 74,600, increase 1,900.
Of. This word is not needed. of Tola. Should be "to Tola [pertained]", as in v. 6. The word "to" or "unto" is read in some codices with Sam. and Sept.
threescore, &c. = 64,300. In Num. 2. 6 = 54,400, increase 9,900.
threescore, &c. = 60,500. In Num. 2. 8 = 57,400, increase 3,100.
Manasseh comes before Ephraim here, because the tribe had increased. In Num. 2. 18, 20 Ephraim comes first, because he was the standard-bearer, and because of the blessing (Gen. 48. 14).
Gilead. Cp. 32. 39, 40 and Josh. 17. 1. Jeezer. In Josh. 17. 2, Abiezer. Only this tribe, and Judah (v. 21) had great-grandsons as "heads". Cp. Gen. 50. 23.
And = Now. daughters. Cp. 27. 1; 36. 1-12; and Josh. 17. 3, 4. Their names are written Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah (some codices, with Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and Milcah"), and Tirzah.
fifty and two, &c. = 52,700. In Num. 2. 21 = 32,200, increase 20,500.

And. Some codices, with Sam., Jon., and Sept., omit "And". Eran ... Eranites. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., and Syr., have "Edan ... Edanites", the letters (Daleth) and (Resh) being easily mistaken.
thirty and two, &c. = 32,500. In Num. 2. 19 = 40,500, decrease 7,500.
of Ard. Ellipsis (Ap. 6) should be supplied thus: "[to Ard] pertained".
forty and five, &c. = 45,600. In Num. 2. 23 = 35,400, increase 10,200.
threescore and four, &c. = 64,400. In Num. 2. 26 = 62,700. Decrease = 1,700.
children = sons.
fifty and three, &c. = 53,400. In Num. 2. 28 = 41,500, increase 11,900.
forty and five, &c. = 45,400. In Num. 2. 30 = 53,400, decrease 8,000.

The total number, accomplishing the command, v. 2. See the Structure, p. 219. six hundred, &c. = 601,730. In Num. 2. 32 = 603,550, total decrease 1,820. In Egypt they increased like fishes, Ex. 1. 7, now they decrease. Cp. Ps. 78. 17-33. Seven tribes increased (Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Manasseh, Benjamin, Dan, Asher), total 59,200, beside the 1,000 Levites. Five tribes decreased (Reuben, Simeon, Gad, Ephraim, and Naphtali), total 61,020. LEAH, increase: in Judah 1,900, Issachar 9,900, Zebulun 3,100, Levi 1,000; and decrease in Reuben 2,770, Simeon 37,100. Total decrease 23,970. RACHEL, increase: in Manasseh 20,500, Benjamin 10,200; and decrease in Ephraim 8,000; total increase 22,700. ZILPAH, increase: in Asher 11,900; and decrease in Gad 5,150; total increase 6,750. BILHAH, increase: in Dan 1,700; and decrease in Naphtali 8,000; total decrease 6,300. So, in the four camps: East camp, all increased; South camp, all decreased; West camp, Benjamin and Manasseh increased, Ephraim decreased; North camp, Dan and Asher increased, Naphtali decreased. On the whole, cp. Job 12. 9, 10, 14, 23.
52-62 (B, p. 200). THEIR INHERITANCE.
many = the greater number. few = the smaller number.

by = "upon": i.e. "contingently upon" (see v. 56). By Eleazar (34. 17), because, as high priest, he had the Urim and Thummim, which were the lots cast. The high priest must be present for the lot to speak, and give Jehovah's decision (Josh. 17. 4). Cp. Ezra 2. 61-63. Neh. 7. 63-65. The lot "came up" (Josh. 18. 11); "came forth" (Josh. 19. 1); "came out" (Josh. 19. 17) of the bag (containing the Urim and Thummin) which was in or behind the breastplate. See note on Ex. 28. 30, and cp. Prov. 16. 33; 18. 18.
the lot = Heb. "the mouth of the lot", as though the "lot" spoke and was personified, by the Fig. Prosopopoeia (Ap. 6). See on v. 55.
Jochebed. Cp. Ex. 2. 1 and 6. 20. bare to Levi in Egypt. This explains apparent discrepancy between her age and that of Amram. See Ap. 50. III.
Nadab. Cp. Lev. 10. 2. Num. 3. 4. 1 Chron. 24. 2.

said. Forty years before. Cp. ch. 14. 28-33. shall surely die. Heb. "a dying they will die". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6). See note on Gen. 2. 17; 26. 28. save Caleb, &c. Cp. 14. 24, 30, 38. The whole congregation therefore composed of men over twenty, and none older than sixty.
27. 1-11 (B, p. 219). INHERITANCE: THE DAUGHTERS OF ZELOPHEHAD. (Alternation.) daughters. Cp. 26. 33. Josh. 17. 3.
door = entrance. tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. Ap. 40.
died. Cp. 26. 64, 65. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. sin. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i.
Why ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
spake. See note on 1. 1.
shalt surely give. Heb. "a giving thou shalt give". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis. See note on Gen. 26. 28. This command obeyed in Josh. 17. 4.
children = sons.
unto his kinsman. Cp. note on Lev. 18. 6. a statute of judgment: or, regulative statute. Cp. 35. 29. as = according to what.
27. 12—31. 54 (B3, p. 176). EVENTS AND LAWS (Introversion). 27. 12-23 (A, above). EVENT: MOSES' SUCCESSOR (Alternation). the LORD said = Jehovah said. See note on 3. 40.
Aaron. Cp. 20. 24.
rebelled. Cp. 20. 24. My commandment. Heb. "My mouth". Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, "mouth" put for what is spoken by it. water. Cp. Ex. 17. 7. Of another Meribah.

God = Elohim. God, the Creator of men and the spirits of men (Gen. 2. 7), Who giveth the spirit to man, and takes it to Himself again (Ecc. 12. 7), and Who giveth all the gifts of the Spirit (1 Cor. 14. 12). spirits. Plural of Heb. ruach. See Ap. 9. set = or visit: i.e. provide and appoint. man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii.
go out ... go in. Fig. Synecdoche (of Species), Ap. 6, put for life in general, especially all official movements, and actions.

said. See note on 3. 40. Joshua. See note on Ex. 17. 9. spirit. Heb. ruach (Ap. 9). Put here by the Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the gifts of the Holy Spirit: here, a spirit of "wisdom" (Deut. 34. 9).
Eleazar the priest: because he had the breastplate with Urim and Thummim, and could alone give Joshua the decision or "judgment" of Jehovah.

he shall stand = take his stand. Heb. 'amad, as v. 2. counsel. Supply Ellipsis with the word "judgment" from next clause (Ap. 6. iii. 1). for = by. after = for. judgment = decision. Urim = the Urim. See note on Ex. 28. 30. at his word = at the mouth: i.e. of the Urim. word = commandment or instruction, "word" put by Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, for what is spoken by the mouth.
commanded = spake. See note on 1. 1. by the hand. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6: i.e. by the instrumentality or agency of the hand.
28. 1—29. 40 (B, p. 222). LAWS AS TO OFFERINGS (Introversion). the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

children = sons. offering = approach offering Heb. korban. Ap. 43. II. i. bread. Fig. Synecdoche (of Species), Ap. 6, put for all kinds of food. sweet savour. See note on Lev. 1. 9. offer = bring near. Heb. karab. Ap. 43. I. i. due season = appointed time. Heb. mo'ed. See note on Gen. 1. 14.
3-31 (n, above). PARTICULAR: AS TO OFFERINGS (Division). without spot. Heb. tamim, without blemish. See Ap. 26.
offer = prepare. Heb. 'asah. Ap. 43. I. iii. at even = between the evenings.
ephah. See Ap. 51. III. 3. meat offering. Heb. minchah = meal or gift offering. Ap. 43. II. iii. hin. See Ap. 51. III. 3.
holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5. strong wine. Heb. shekar. Ap. 27. iv.
beside = over and above.
offer = bring near. Heb. karav. Ap. 43. I. i.
tenth deals. See Ap. 51. III. 3.
wine. Heb. yayin. Ap. 27. 1.
sin offering. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 43. II. v.
fourteenth. Cp. Ex. 12. 2, 14, 18. Lev. 23. 5. first. Cp. Lev. 23. 7.
atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33.
beside = in addition to, as in v. 31 (not "upon", as in vv. 10 and 24).
in the day = at the time. See Ap. 18. after your weeks be out = on the eve of your weeks.
one. Some codices, with one early printed edition, Sam., Jon., and Syr., read "and one".
two. Some codices, with one early printed edition, Sam., Sept., and Syr., read "and two".
And. This word, "and", is read in some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg.

29. 1-38 (n, p. 223). PARTICULAR: re SEVENTH MONTH (Division). seventh month. Heb. name Tisri not known in Scripture (our Sept.-Oct.). The old civil year went out (Ex. 23. 16; 34. 22), known as Ethanim (1 Kings 8. 2). Tisri = the first month of civil year. Nisan, or Abib = the first month of sacred year. holy. See note on Ex. 3. 5. servile = laborious. blowing the trumpets. Cp. Lev. 23. 24.
offer = prepare. Heb. 'asah. Ap. 43. I. iii. sweet savour. See note on Lev. 1. 9. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. without blemish = physically perfect. See Ap. 26.
meat offering. See Ap. 43. II. iii. tenth deals. See Ap. 51. III. 3.
sin offering. See Ap. 43. II. v. atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33.
Beside = in addition to. See note on 28. 23. manner = ordinance, or regulation.
souls. Plural of Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13.
offer = bring near. Heb. karav. Ap. 43. I. i.
A several tenth. Heb. "a tenth, a tenth" = a tenth severally, i.e. to each.
One. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "And one". the sin offering of atonement. This was the great offering of the day of atonement. Lev. 16.
fifteenth day. The Feast of Tabernacles. the seventh month. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "this month".
a several tenth. As in v. 10, but the second word "tenth" has the extraordinary points (Ap. 31) omitting the word, making it like v. 4, instead of like v. 10.
his meat offering = the meal offering thereof. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and the", or "and his".
ye shall offer. The Ellipsis (Ap. 6) is correctly supplied from preceding verses (vv. 2, 8, 13).
Their. Some codices, with one early printed edition, Sam., Sept., and Syr., read "And their".
his. See note on v. 16. Some codices, with Sam., Onk., Syr., and Vulg., read "and his".
his. See note on v. 16. Some codices, with one early printed edition, Sam., Onk., and Syr., read "and his". drink offering. Some codices have this in the plural.
solemn assembly. Cp. Lev. 23. 36.
Their. Some codices, with Sam., Syr., and Vulg., read "With their".
set feasts = appointed seasons. See note on 28. 2 and Gen. 1. 14.
children = sons.
30. 1-16 (B, p. 222). LAWS AS TO VOWS. (Introversion.) heads = rulers or princes. children = sons. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.

man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. vow a vow. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6) = make a solemn promise. soul. Heb. nephesh (Ap. 13), used in this chapter twelve times for the whole (responsible) person. break = Heb. profane.
3-15 (r, above). VOWS MADE BY WOMEN. (Alternation.) and = or. bind ... a bond. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6) = make a solemn bond.
shall stand = abideth firm. Cp. Gen. 23. 17, 20. Ps. 19. 7. Isa. 14. 24; 40. 8. Jer. 44. 29.
her. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "all her", as in v. 4.
divorced. Heb. "put away [from her husband]". Cp. Lev. 21. 7.
hath utterly made them void. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6). Heb. "a making void he hath made them void". Fig. well represented by the word "utterly". See note on Gen. 26. 28.
altogether, &c. Heb. "a holding his peace, he held his peace". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), well translated by "altogether".
iniquity. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the punishment occasioned by it. Heb. 'avah. Ap. 44. iv.
31. 1-54 (A, p. 222). EVENT: MOSES' VENGEANCE ON MIDIANITES (Alternation). the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

Avenge. Heb. revenge the revengement. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6). = execute due vengeance. children = sons. afterward. Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg. read "and afterward". be gathered, &c. Cp. 27. 13.
avenge the LORD of Midian = render the vengeance of Jehovah upon Midian. Cp. ch. 25. 17.
armed = assigned to or for, &c.
Phinehas. Cp. 25. 7-15. instruments = vessels. trumpets = alarm trumpets, which were also prayer trumpets. Cp. 10. 9, 10.
as = according as.
Evi. Cp. Josh. 13. 21. five kings: called princes or dukes of Sihon, Josh. 13. 21. Balaam. Cp. Josh. 13. 22. slew. Balaam thus did not "die the death of the righteous". Cp. 23. 10.
burnt = burnt up, or down. Heb. saraph. Ap. 43. I. viii. The same judgment is in store for spiritual fornication. Rev. 17. 16; 18. 8. castles = fortified places.
prey = booty. Heb. malkoah. First occurrence. Always used of animated prey. men. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. I.
captives. Heb. captivity. the. Some codices, with Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "all the".
meet them: as Melchizedek met Abram (Gen. 14. 17).
wroth. Moses meek in his own matters, but not in Jehovah's. In these there was a "godly jealousy". battle. Heb. battle of the war = "the [battle] array (or host) of the war", or martial host.
these. Cp. 25. 2. counsel = word, or doctrine (Rev. 2. 14). trespass = Heb. ma'al. Cp. Ap. 44. xi.
man. Heb. 'ish (Ap. 14. II). him = male.
person = soul. Heb. nephesh (Ap. 13).
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14. went = came, or had come. ordinance = statute.
the. Some codices, with Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and the" in each of these three instances, making the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6). iron. Found in Egypt as early as 2800 B.C.
water of separation. See ch. 19.
spake. See note on 1. 1.
man. Heb 'adam. Ap. 14. I.
tribute = computed value, assigned to Jehovah. Heb. mekes. Occurs only in this chapter. soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. persons = men. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. I.
give it. An extra portion in addition to Deut. 18. 1, 2 and Num. 18. 19. So Abram, Gen. 14. 20.
of the. Some codices, with Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and of the". tabernacle = habitation. Heb. mishkan. Ap. 40.
as = according as.
beeves. Old English (from the French), for oxen.
persons. Heb. pl. of nephesh. Ap. 13. III. note man = male.
to war = to, or, for the host.
And the persons. Fig. Epanadiplosis. Ap. 6. persons = souls. Heb. nephesh (pl.). Ap. 13. Lit. soul of man (Ap. 14. I).
gave them. See 1 Chron. 9. 2. Heb. nathan, to give. Hence their name, "Nethinim."
oblation. This was voluntary. The levy in v. 25, &c., was commanded. See Lev. 2. 4. jewels = instruments or vessels. atonement. See note on Ex. 29. 33. souls. Heb. pl. of nephesh. Ap. 13.
offering = heave offering. See Ap. 43. II. viii., and note on Ex. 29. 27. offered up = heaved. shekels. See Ap. 51. II.
tabernacle = tent. Heb. 'ohel. See Ap. 40.

32. 1—36. 13 (A4, p. 176). DIVISION OF LAND: JOURNEYINGS AND ORDER (SETTLEMENT). (Introversion.) 32. 1-42 (B, above). DIVISION: EAST OF JORDAN (Repeated Alternation). children = sons. cattle. In Heb. this verse begins and ends with the word "cattle". Fig. Epanadiplosis (Ap. 6), to emphasise the first cause of this division. behold. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6), to strengthen the emphasis.

Ataroth, &c. These were the places in the countries of Sihon and Og, on the east of Jordan. Cp. Josh. 16. 2, 5, 7. Dibon. Cp. 21. 30. Josh. 13. 9, 17. Nimrah. Called Beth-nimrah, v. 36, and Nimrim. Isa. 15. 6. Cp. Josh. 13. 27. Heshbon. 21. 26. Josh. 13. 17. Shebam. Called Shibmah, v. 38. Cp. Josh. 13. 19. Isa. 16. 8, 9. Jer. 48. 32. Beon. Called Baal-meon, v. 38; Beth-meon, Jer. 48. 23; and Beth-baal-meon, Josh. 13. 17.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. is. Heb "it [is]".
Eshcol. Cp. 13. 23, 24.
the same time. Heb. "on that day".
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. unto Abraham, &c. All three mentioned together here as equally subjects of the oath of Jehovah. Cp. Gen. 50. 24.
the generation: or, the men of that generation. evil. Heb. ra'a'. Ap. 44. VIII.
behold. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6), to emphasise what follows. increase = a crew, multitude, or brood. sinful. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. i.
leave them: or leave them behind.
will not return. Promise fulfilled (Josh. 22. 3, 4). man. Heb. 'ish (Ap. 14).

spake. Heb. text reads sing., "he spake", and by Fig. Heterosis (of Number), Ap. 6, might be translated plural, "they spake". But "they spake" is the actual reading in several codices: Sam., Jon., Onk., Sept., Syr., and Vulg. It is also the Sevir reading. See Ap. 34. as = according as.
will pass over. Cp. Josh. 4. 12.
every man = all.

armed ... they. Between these two words the Sept. has "to do battle before Jehovah, then shall ye bring over their baggage, and their wives, and their cattle earlier than you into the land of Canaan; so shall" (they have possession), &c.

32. 33-42 [For Structure see next page]. 32. 33-42 (x4, p. 228). COMPLIANCE OF MOSES (GRANT TO THE TWO-AND-A-HALF TRIBES). (Extended Alternation.) Moses gave. Cp. Deut. 3. 12. Josh. 13. 8; 22. 4. coasts = borders, or confines.
Jair. In the Heb. this verse begins and ends with the word "Jair". Fig. Epanadiplosis (Ap. 6). Havoth = the encampments, or tent villages (of Jair).
villages. Heb. daughters; depending on the mother or metropolitan city. Fig. Prosopopoeia (Ap. 6).
33. 1-49 (C, p. 228). JOURNEYINGS. (Division.) 33. 1-15 (b1, above). FIRST PERIOD. journeys. Heb. pullings up: i.e. of the tent-pegs, or the breakings up of the camps. children = sons.
wrote. See note on Ex. 17. 14, and Ap. 47. commandment. Heb. "mouth", put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause) for what is spoken by it (Ap. 6). the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
the Egyptians: repeated = Fig. Anadiplosis (Ap. 6).
upon their gods. Cp. Ex. 12. 12; 18. 8, 11.

before Pi-hahiroth. Heb. text and R.V. = "before Hahiroth"; but this differs from the other two occurrences of the name (Ex. 14. 2, 9), in all three of which it is Pi-hahiroth. A special various reading called Sevir (Ap. 34) has the full name Pi-hahiroth in this verse. The A.V. has kept the Pi as well, and made it "before Pi-". It should, perhaps, read here, as in every other case in this chapter, "from Pi-hahiroth".
by the Red sea. Not named before.
wilderness of Sin. Ex. 16. 1, 2.
Dophkah. Not named before.
Alush. Not named before.
Rephidim. Cp. Ex. 17.
wilderness of Sinai. Cp. Ex. 19. 1. Acts 7. 38.
33. 16-17 (b2, above). SECOND PERIOD. Kibroth-hattaavah. Cp. 11. 4-34.
Hazeroth. Cp. Num. 11. 35.
33. 18-36 (b3, above). THIRD PERIOD (NO HISTORY). Rithmah. Cp. 13. 1-3. Whence the spies went to view the land: means "Juniper": well named for the evil tongues of the spies. Cp. Ps. 120. 3, 4.
Rimmon-parez. Not named before.
Libnah. Perhaps the Laban of Deut. 1. 1.
Rissah. Not elsewhere mentioned.
Jotbathah. Cp. Deut. 10. 7.
Ezion-gaber. Cp. Deut. 2. 8. Edom's seaport on the Red Sea.
33. 37-49 (b4, p. 230). FOURTH PERIOD.
fortieth year. The number of Probation (Ap. 10).
died. Cp. 20. 24, 26, &c., born 1575 B.C. mount Hor. Cp. 21. 4.
king Arad. Cp. 21. 1-3.
Ije-abarim = heaps, or ruins, of Abarim. "Iim", v. 45, probably an abbreviation.
Dibon-gad = Dibon of the tribe of Gad. Cp. Num. 21. 30. So called because it was appropriated by Gad (32. 34); and to distinguish it from another Dibon given to Reuben (Josh. 13. 15, 17).
Nebo. Where Moses died. Deut. 32. 49, 50; 34. 1, 5.
33. 50—36. 12 (B, p. 228). DIVISION WEST OF JORDAN (Alternation). spake. See note on 1. 1.
33. 51—34. 29 (d, above). THE LAND OF CANAAN (Division). 33. 51—34. 15 (e1, above). THE DIVISION. (Extended Alternation.)
drive out. This was one of the great purposes for which the sword of Israel was raised up. Cp. Deut. 7. 1, 2. Ex. 23. 33. See App. 23 and 25.
inhabitants of the land. Fig. Ellipsis (Ap. 6) correctly supplied. Heb. "land" is put by Fig. Metonymy (of Subject), Ap. 6, for the inhabitants.
ye shall divide. Cp. 26. 53.
not drive out. Alas! they did not. Cp. Josh. 13. 13; 15. 63; 16. 10. Judg. 1. 19, 21, 28, 29, 30-36; 2. 1-5. See Ap. 25. pricks. Cp. Josh. 23. 13. = for pricks. Cp. Ezek. 28. 24. Judg. 2. 3.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.
children = sons. When ye come. After the final command (above) follow instructions as to the quiet possession of the land thus cleared of enemies. coasts = borders, or confines.
south quarter. Cp. Josh. 15. 1. Begins at east corner. salt sea. So v. 12.
Akrabbim = Maaleh-akrabbim. Josh. 15. 3. = the ascent of scorpions. Cp. Deut. 8. 15. going forth = ascending. Cp. Josh. 15. 3
river. Heb. nachal, a wady; not nahar, a river. Here used of "Sihor", and called the river of Egypt. Cp. Gen. 15. 18, where it is nahar = the Nile.

great sea: i.e. the Mediterranean, a modern name for the Great Sea. point out = mark out or claim. Heb. ta'ah. Occurs only here. mount Hor. Not the mount Hor where Aaron died, which was in the south corner of Edom (33. 37, 38), but another, in the north, mount Hermon, a spur of the Lebanon (Josh. 13. 5). Hermon had several names. Cp. Deut. 3. 9; 4. 48.
Hamath. In Amos 6. 2 called "Hamath the great", mentioned as in the north border.

Riblah. A city in Hamath, where God executed His judgment on two kings of Judah and others (2 Kings 23. 33; 25. 6, 20, 21. Jer. 39. 5, 6). Chinnereth. Cp. Josh. 12. 3; 13. 27. In New Testament "the sea of Galilee" and "sea of Tiberias" (John 6. 1); also "the lake of Gennesaret" (Luke 5. 1).
For the tribe. Cp. 32. 33. Josh. 14. 2, 3.

These are the names. Cp. 13. 2-16. See Ap. 45. men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. Eleazar. Because he was the high priest, and had the breastplate with the lots, the "Urim and Thummim." See notes on Ex. 28. 30 and Num. 26. 55. Josh. 17. 4. See also Num. 27. 21.
Caleb. The only one of the spies, beside Joshua, left, ch. 13. 6, 30, and cp. 14. 24. Josh. 14. 6, &c.
These. See the order of the tribes in Ap. 45.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. spake. See note on 1. 1.

35. 2—36. 12 (d, p. 231). THE LAND OF CANAAN (Division). 2-34 (i1, above). THE LEVITICAL CITIES. (Alternation.) In this Structure the cities are given in Alternation; their number in an Introversion. children = sons. that they give. Jehovah gives to the Nation; the Nation gives to the Levites.
suburbs = pasture grounds.
cubits. See Ap. 51. III. 2.
to them. A special various reading called Sevir (Ap. 34) reads "to you", with which agree some codices, Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and one early printed edition.
six cities. See Deut. 4. 41. Josh. 20. 2, 7, 8; 21. 3.

forty and eight cities. Cp. Josh. 21. 41. So was Gen 49. 5, 7 fulfilled, that Levi should be "divided in Jacob and scattered in Israel". At first a curse, but changed to a blessing on account of Ex. 32. 26, 29.

according to his inheritance. Nine from Judah and Simeon; four from Benjamin; four from Ephraim; four from Dan; two from the half of Manasseh; two from the other half; four from Issachar; four from Asher; three from Naphtali; four from Zebulon; four from Reuben; four from Gad. Cp. Josh. 21. 9, 16, &c.
9-34 (l, above). CITIES OF REFUGE: DESCRIPTION (Alternation).
When ye be come. Cp. Deut. 19. 2. Josh. 20. 2.
person = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. at unawares = by misadventure.

avenger. Heb. Goel, to redeem, to ransom. First occurrence is Gen. 48. 16; next, Ex. 6. 6; 15. 13. Goel, when used in this connection, means to avenge bloodshed, as here; both were the duties of the next of kin, the kinsman. Our Goel not only redeems us from all evil, but avenges us of all our enemies. Rom. 8. 31-34.

three cities = Bezer, Ramoth, Golan (Deut. 4. 41-43). and three = Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron (Josh. 20. 7). These were placed in due order, east and west, in two ranks: Hebron over against Bezer. Shechem over against Ramoth. Kedesh over against Golan. If the Lord enlarged their land, they were to add three more (Deut. 19. 8, 9).
-15-34 [For Structure see next page]. -15-34 (n, p. 233). PURPOSE. (Alternation.) person = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13.
revenger of blood. See note on v. 12.
of hatred. Deut. 19. 11, 12. laying of wait = fixing the eyes upon. Heb. zediyyah. Occurs only here and v. 22.
without enmity. Cp. Ex. 21. 13.
was not his enemy. Heb. "he not [being] his enemy".
26-34 (p, above). NEGATIVE PURPOSE. (Alternation.)
statute of judgment = a regulative ordinance. Cp. 27. 11. dwellings = dwelling-places.
person = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. mouth. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the evidence given by it.

no satisfaction = no ransom. Cp. Ps. 49. 7. Only God can redeem (v. 15). life = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. which is guilty of death = if he has unlawfully caused death: "guilty" being put by Fig. Metonymy (of Effect), Ap. 6, for the crime which has caused it. Heb. "wicked, to die".
priest: i.e. the high priest. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., and Syr., read it so, as in v. 28.
wherein ye are. Some codices, with Sam., Syr., and Vulg., read "wherein ye are dwelling". blood: i.e. blood unlawfully shed. him that shed it. Cp. Gen. 9. 6.
Defile not = Defile thou not. Some codices, with Sam., Onk., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "Defile ye not". wherein = in the midst of which. among = in the midst of.
36. 1-12 (i2, p. 233). HEIRESSES. (Alternation.) chief fathers = heads. sons. A special various reading called Sevir (Ap. 34), with Syr., reads "son", as in v. 12. children = sons.
The LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. my lord = Moses, to whom the commandment was given. 26. 52, 53, &c.; 27. 6, 7.
jubile. Cp. Lev. 25.
word. Heb. mouth. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for what is spoken by it.
keep himself = cleave.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. II.
These. This verse forms the closing Epilogue to the whole book of Numbers.

lines.label: C

lines.label: A

34. 1-7 (D, p. 236). Moses' Death and Burial (Introversion and Alternation)

prose.text: TITLE. Moses. See Ap. 2 and 47. Called: by the Sept. translators, and from them by Jerome, in the Vulgate. Deuteronomy = Second Law, from 17. 18, where "copy of the law" is so rendered from Rabbinic mishneh, a doubling. Hebrew Title = Hadd'barim = "the words". It is the fifth book, concluding the five books of the Pentateuch (see Ap. 10). No scroll of the Pentateuch ever seen with more than these five. See Ap. 46 and 47. The whole history of the book took place in the eleventh month of the fortieth year. Only the last fifteen chapters of Numbers refer to the time of Deut.

These. Note the ten (see Ap. 10) addresses by Moses:— 1. 1. 6—4. 40. 2. 5. 1—10. 5. 3. 10. 10—12. 32. 4. 13. 1—26. 19. 5. 27. 1—28. 68. 6. 29. 2—30. 20. 7. 31. 2-6. 8. 32. 1-43. 9. 32. 44-47. 10. 33. 2-29. the words = Hadd'barim. See note above. all Israel. Cp. 5. 1. Mode given by God, Ex. 3. 16; 4. 29. Lev. 24. 14. "All" used by Fig. Synecdoche (Ap. 6) to signify a national gathering of any size (1 Sam. 7. 3; 12. 1, 19. 1 Kings 8. 2, 14, 22, 55, 62; 12. 12, 16, 18, &c.). this side Jordan = across Jordan, a neutral term, expression to be determined by context. Num. 22. 1. the plain. Heb. 'Arabah = name of vale from Jordan to gulf of Akabah. Red sea = Suph, name of a place. Omit "sea". See Num. 33. 48, 49, 50; 35. 1; 36. 13.
eleven days': i.e. going direct. Seir = Edom. Kadesh-barnea. See Num. 32. 8.

fortieth. The number of Probation. See Ap. 10. First month, Miriam died, Num. 20. 1; fifth month, Aaron died, Num. 33. 38; at the end, Moses died on 29 Sebat, 1452; for the thirty days' mourning end with last day of the fortieth year (29 Adar, 1452). See Ap. 50, vii. 3, 4. children = sons. according unto, &c. Always thus. Cp. 2 Pet. 1. 20, 21. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
and Og. Fig. Ellipsis (Ap. 6. iii. 1) = "and [had slain] Og". Cp. Num. 21. 34, 35. in Edrei. Some codices, with Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and in". Cp. Josh. 12. 4.

began = undertook with will. Heb ya'al. First occurrence Gen 18. 27, 31. declare. Heb. ba'ar, make plain, show sense, set forth, especially in writing. Occurs only here and 27. 8, and Hab. 2. 2. law = torah = instruction.

1. 6—32. 47. [For Structures see next page.] 1. 6—32. 47 (C, p. 236). THE TRIBES. THEIR ADMINISTRATION. (Alternation and Introversion.) 1. 6—3. 29 (G, above). POSSESSION EAST OF JORDAN: RETROSPECTIVE (Extended Alternation). The LORD our God = Jehovah 'eloheinu. Two titles of later date do not occur in Deut.: "The LORD of hosts" (Samuel) and "the Holy One of Israel" (Isaiah). spake. Jehovah spake only here to "us". His speaking to others, see 2. 1. Jehovah "said", see 2. 9. Jehovah "commanded", see 4. 14. Horeb. Twentieth day of second month. Num. 10. 11-13.

Turn you = Face about. Note the Fig. Polyonymia (Ap. 6) in this verse. Heb. panah, set one's face; start. vale. Heb. Shephelah = Philistia. south. Heb. Negeb, the hill country south of Judea. See note on "South", Gen. 12. 9; 13. 1. river. Heb. nahar, a flood, not nahal, a wady. Cp. Gen. 15. 18. the river. Fig. Anadiplosis. Ap. 6.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6). Abraham. Gen. 15. 18; 17. 7, 8; 24. 7; 26. 3, &c. This promise mentioned twenty-seven times in Deut., but unintelligible without Genesis.
1. 9-45. [For Structure see next page.] 9-45 (f, above). DISOBEDIENCE REHEARSED. (Repeated Alternation.) I spake. See Ex. 18. 17, 18. Num. 11. 14.
multiplied. Cp. 10. 22.
as = according as. promised. See Gen. 12. 2; 22. 17, &c.
How. See note on Lam. 1. 1. cumbrance. Heb. torah, only here and Isa. 1. 14 (trouble).

men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. tribes. Heb. shebet, tribe, according to historical or political corporation; always this word in Deut. Where "tribe" is genealogical or geographical elsewhere it is matteh.
I took. Cp. Ex. 18. 21-26. chief. Heb. sar. Cp. Gen. 32. 28. men. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. II.

respect = recognise. persons. Heb. faces. Fig. Synecdoche (of Part), Ap. 6, put for persons. Cp. Lev. 19. 15. judgment. Heb. the judgment: i.e. suited to each case. Cp. Ex. 18. 26. is God's = it [is] God's.
wilderness = desert. Cp. Num. 10. 11-36; 11. 5; 12. 16; 13. 26; and ch. 8. 15. as = according as. Kadesh-barnea. Cp. Num. 32. 8. A place of solemn import in Israel's history.
Amorites = descendants of the Nephilim. See Ap. 25.

every one, &c. = all of you. See note on v. 1. We will send, &c. Proposal came from people, and is here charged home against them. Jehovah assented, and this assent appears in the history. Num. 13. 1-3. men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14.
Eshcol = a cluster of grapes. Num. 13. 22-25.
good land. Cp. Num. 13. 27.
commandment. Heb. mouth. Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the word spoken by it. So v. 43. Ex. 17. 1. Gen. 24. 57, &c.
murmured. Heb. ragan, to rebel. Only here, Ps. 106. 25, and Isa. 29. 24. Amorites. The Severus codex reads "the Amorite" (sing.). See Ap. 34. destroy = exterminate. Heb. shamad.

our brethren = our own brethren. Cp. Num. 13. 28. heart. Some codices, with one early printed edition, read "hearts" (pl.). taller = greater. Some codices, with Sam. and Sept., read "more in number". walled, &c. Fig. Hyperbole. Ap. 6. Anakims. First occurrence; elsewhere, 2. 10, 11, 21; 9. 2. Josh. 11. 21, 22; 14. 12, 15. See Ap. 25. For "sons of Anak", see note on Num. 13. 22.
son. See Num. 11. 11, 12, and cp. Isa. 63. 9 and Acts 13. 18.
the LORD. Heb. "in the LORD" (= Jehovah).

a place. See Ex. 15. 17. Num. 10. 33. Josh. 3. 3, 4. Ezek. 20. 6. your tents. Not only your inheritance, but the halting-place for daily journeying thither. Both were and are Jehovah's choice for His People. in fire by night. See Ex. 13. 21, 22. Num. 10. 33, 34.
was wroth. See Num. 14. 20-35 and Ps. 95. 8-11.
Caleb. Cp. Num. 14. 23, 24. Josh. 14. 9. Judg. 1. 20. children = sons.
This and the next verse are put in a Parenthesis (Ap. 6). angry. See Num. 20. 12.
Joshua. Num. 14. 30.
your little ones. Num. 14. 31.
turn you = start. Num. 14. 25. Red sea = eastern arm. The gulf of Akabah. Cp. v. 1.

answered and said. Idiom. Ap. 6. In this idiom the word "answered" receives its meaning from the context. Here it = confessed, or repented and said. sinned. Heb. chat'a. Ap. 44. I. we will go up. Cp. Num. 14. 40-42. ready. Heb. hun. Occurs only here: = rash, or presumptuous.
rebelled. Num. 14. 44, 45. commandment. Heb. mouth. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, put for what is uttered by it, as in v. 26.
Amorites. Cp. Num. 14. 43. See Ap. 25. bees. Heb. with art. "the bees". Art. of species. destroyed you = beat you down. Heb. kathath.
abode in Kadesh. This is not a summary of the thirty-eight years' wandering, but of what happened before then. How solemn the word "abode" when the command had been "go up".

turned = faced about. Cp. 1. 7. as = according as. the LORD spake. Jehovah spake at nine "sundry times" and in three "divers manners": 1. To me (Moses), 2. 1, 2, 17; 9. 13; 32. 48. 2. To you, 4. 12, 15; 10. 4. 3. To all your assembly, 5. 22. spake = said, as in 1. 42. Cp. Num. 21. 4. many days. These are distinguished from those mentioned in 1. 46. Those were resting in disobedience, these were journeying in obedience.

2. 4—3. 28. [For Structure see next page.] 2. 4—3. 28 (f, p. 238). OBEDIENCE REHEARSED. (Extended and Repeated Alternation.) pass through = cross the border. Num. 20. 4, 14-17. Judg. 11. 17. children = sons.

because, &c. Cp. Gen. 32. 3; 33. 6-8; 36. 8. Josh. 24. 4. a possession. Heb. yarash (because given). Also in vv. 9, 12, and 3. 19, 20, &c.; in Deut. not 'ahaz (because seized), as in other books; though 'ahaz is used in ch. 32. 49.
meat. Put by Fig. Synecdoche (Ap. 6) for all kinds of food.

the LORD thy God. Jehovah thy Elohim = the triune God. hand. Some codices, with some early printed editions, and Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "hands". forty years. Cp. Neh. 9. 21. nothing. Heb. "not a word": i.e. of what Jehovah had promised. Cp. 8. 2-4.
passed by. Cp. Num. 20. 21; 21. 11-13. 2 Chron. 20. 10. from Elath, &c. Gulf of Akabah. Cp. Num. 33. 35, 36, and 1 Kings 9. 26. wilderness of Moab. See the route, Judg. 11. 16-18.

the LORD [Heb. Jehovah] said unto me (or Moses). Occurs thirteen times in Deut.: 2. 9, 31; 3. 2, 26; 4. 10; 5. 28; 9. 12; 10. 1, 11; 18. 17; 31. 2, 14, 16; 34. 4. Distress not, &c. God judged both (2 Chron. 20. 1-25. Amos 1. 13-15).
Emims = terrible ones (Gen. 14. 5). A race of the Nephilim. See Ap. 25. Anakims. See on 1. 28, and Ap. 25.
giants. Heb. Rephaim, another name for the Nephilim, from one Rapha. See Ap. 25. Connected with healing, and with Egypt (Gen. 50. 2). See Ap. 23.

Horims. Another race or name of the Nephilim. See Ap. 25. Cp. Gen. 14. 6. See Ap. 25. destroyed = exterminated. Heb. shamad. stead = room. These are the Canaanites with whom Satan had preoccupied the land to thwart God's purpose in Abraham. Cp. Gen. 12. 6; 13. 7, and see Ap. 25. All these had to be destroyed, as the Nephilim were destroyed by the Flood. Cp. Gen. 6. 4, which tells of a later irruption. See Gen. 14. 5. possession ... gave. See ch. 3. 20, and note on v. 5.
Now. Some codices, with Sam. and Sept., read "Now therefore". brook Zered, which flows into the Arnon, the frontier between Moab and Ammon. Num. 21. 13.
thirty and eight years. Cp. the antitype of Israel in the flesh, John 5. 5.
destroy = shake off. Heb. hamam.
Ammon. See Gen. 19. 36-38, and cp. Judg. 11. 15.
Zamzummims. A name given them by the Ammonites = noisy ones. See vv. 10-12, and Ap. 25.
Anakims. See note on 1. 28, and Ap. 25.
destroyed = exterminated. Heb. shamad.

Avims. Another name for these Nephilim. Josh. 13. 3. (Ap. 25.) Azzah = Gaza. Gen. 10. 19. 1 Sam. 6. 17. Cp. 1 Kings 4. 24. Jer. 25. 20. Acts 8. 26. Caphtorims. Another name, for those that came out of Caphtor. Gen. 10. 14. Amos 9. 7. Jer. 47. 4. Sometimes identified with Crete, or the Delta.
take your journey. Cp. Num. 21. 13.
put the dread. Fulfilment of Ex. 15. 14, 15. Cp. Josh. 2. 9, 10.
sent messengers. Num. 21. 21, 22. Judg. 11. 19. Kedemoth. Cp. Num. 21. 21-24. Afterward a Levitical city (Josh. 13. 18; 21. 37. 1 Chron. 6. 64, 79).

shalt sell. Edom refused to let Israel pass through, but did sell, as here stated. Cp. Num. 20. 17-21. Moab, too, "sold", but did not meet as a friend (23. 4, where karam means to offer unasked). Cp. Isa. 21. 17.
As = According as.

2. 30—3. 29 (m3, p. 241). FORMER INHABITANTS (Division). Sihon ... would not. Cp. Num. 21. 23. Judg. 11. 20. God = Elohim, acting as the Creator with a creature. See Ap. 4. hardened. Heb. kashah. See note on Ex. 4. 21. spirit = Heb. ruach. See Ap. 9.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
came out. Sihon was the aggressor. Num. 21. 23. Judg. 11. 20.
sons. So read, but written in Heb. text "son" (sing.).
destroyed = devoted to destruction. Heb. haram. Cp. 3. 6; 7. 2; 20. 17. men. Heb. m'thim. See Ap. 14. v.
a prey. For the law governing this see Num. 31.
Aroer. Num. 32. 34. The name is on the Moabite Stone. See Ap. 54. the city: i.e. Ar of Moab. Num. 21. 15. delivered. Cp. Judg. 11. 21, 22, 26. "For His mercy endureth for ever", Ps. 136. 18-22.
3. 1-29 (M2, above). THE CONQUEST OF OG. (Introversion.) Bashan. Cp. Num. 21. 33, 34. came out. Og was the aggressor. Num. 21. 33.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. said. See note on 2. 9. hand. Some codices, with three early printed editions, Sept., and Vulg., read "hands". as = according as.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. I. delivered. Cp. 2. 36.

threescore cities. They can all be seen, and counted to-day. (See Dr. Porter's Giant Cities of Bashan.) region. Heb. = "cord". Put by Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for the region marked out by it. Argob. Cp. 1 Kings 4. 13. Ps. 136. 18-22.
cities. See note on v. 4.
destroyed ... destroying = devoted to destruction. Heb. haram. Cp. 7. 2. men. Heb. m'thim = adult males. Ap. 14. v. women. Some codices, with Jon., Sept., Syr., and Vulg., read "and the women".
spoil. For laws regulating this, see Num. 31.
on this side = across, a neutral term. See note on 1. 1. unto. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., and Syr., read "and (or even) unto". Hermon = high mountain.
Which. Note these topographical parentheses, vv. 9, 11, 14, cp. 2. 20-23, 29. Sirion = breastplate. Shenir = coat of mail.
Gilead = the rough country.

giants. Heb. "Rephaim", descendants of one Rapha, a branch of the Nephilim. See Ap. 25. behold. A special various reading called Sevir (see Ap. 34) reads "and behold". bedstead = bed or couch, but not the usual word which is mishkab. It is 'eres, and is exactly the same measurement as the tomb of Marduk in Babylon. The mythological significance of 'eres (Bab. irsu) is nuptial bed, or funeral couch. Probably = tomb. iron. Probably basalt. is it not ...? Fig. Erotesis (Ap. 6), for emphasis. Rabbath was the capital of Ammon, where the temple of Milchom was: and where Og's tomb would naturally be. children = sons. cubits. See Ap. 51. III. 2. cubit of a man = a common cubit = a man's forearm. man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. II.

coasts = borders. Bashan-havoth-jair = the villages (or cluster of villages) of Jair in Bashan. Heb. Havoth = towns, used only of Jair's. Cp. Num. 32. 41. Josh. 13. 30. Judg. 10. 4. 1 Kings 4. 13. 1 Chron. 2. 23. unto this day: unto the time of writing. Here the time mentioned is from Num. 21 to the eleventh month of the fortieth year (Deut. 1. 3).

Chinnereth. Afterward called Gennesaret, cp. Num. 34. 11. Josh. 19. 35. So called from its shape, kinnor, a harp. the plain. Heb. 'Arabah. See 1. 1. Ashdoth-pisgah = the springs of Pisgah. Note the Fig. Polyonymia (Ap. 6) in this verse.

18-28 (n, p. 241). COMMANDS OF MOSES. (Alternation.) I commanded. See Num. 32. 20-24. meet for the war. Heb. = sons of valour. Fig. Antimereia (of Noun), Ap. 6 = valiant men. Emphasis on valiant. Cp. 2 Sam. 2. 7. 1 Kings 1. 52.
return. Cp. Josh. 22. 4.

Lord GOD = Adonai Jehovah. See Ap. 4. This prayer not mentioned elsewhere. hand. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, put for works wrought by the hand. GOD. Heb 'El. = God as the omnipotent One. See Ap. 4. IV.
the good land. Cp. Ps. 106. 24. Num. 13. 27.
wroth. See Num. 20. 12. said. See note on 2. 9.

westward, &c. The points of the compass here are seaward, darkness-ward, Teman-ward, and sunrise-ward. Teman-ward (i.e. south of Edom) first used for south in Ex. 26. 18. See Num. 27. 12. and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton, Ap. 6, emphasising the extent of the view. not go over. Cp. Num. 27. 13.
charge Joshua. Cp. Num. 27. 18, 19.

Beth-peor = the house (or temple) of Peor, where Baal was worshipped (Num. 23. 28; 25. 3. Deut. 4. 3. Here Moses was buried (Deut. 34. 6). It was a Moabite holy place (Num. 25. 18; 31. 16. Josh. 22. 17). Allotted to Reuben (Josh. 13. 20).

4. 1—5. 33 (a, p. 238). INJUNCTIONS IN HOREB: RETROSPECTIVE (Introversion and Alternation). 4. 1-8 (N, above). STATUTES ANNOUNCED. (Extended alternation.) statutes = ordinances: Godward. Ex. 12. 24, 43; 30. 21. Heb. 9. 1. judgments = duties and punishments, manward. First occurrence in plural in Ex. 21. 1. The two often united. See 5. 1; 6. 1; 12. 1. Mal. 4. 4, &c. teach. Heb. lamad (whence "Talmud") = to cause to learn. First occurrence. for to do. Old English idiom: modern idiom = to do. the LORD God = Jehovah 'Elohim.
Ye shall not add. Cp. ch. 12. 32. Prov. 30. 5, 6. Jer. 23. 28; 26. 2. Ezek. 2. 5, 7. Rev. 22. 18, 19.
men. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. II. Baal-peor. See note on 3. 29 and Num. 25. 1-5, 9. Ps. 106. 28. Hos. 9. 10. 1 Cor. 10. 8. destroyed = exterminated. Heb. shmadh.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
understanding = discernment. understanding = discerning.
what ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. God = a god, or gods. Heb. 'Elohim. Ap. 4. I. nigh = nigh to help. Cp. Ps. 32. 9; 34. 18; 119. 151; 145. 18. Neh. 13. 4.
so righteous. See Ap. 15. Cp. 2 Sam. 7. 23.
9-20 (r, above). WARNINGS AGAINST IDOLATRY. (Alternation.) take heed. Note the three occurrences in this chapter (vv. 9, 15, 23). thy soul = thyself. Heb. thy nephesh, cp. yourselves, v. 15. Ap. 13.

Specially. Fig. Ellipsis. Ap. 6. Might be supplied by the word "Remember". Horeb. Occurs three times before Deut. (viz. Ex. 3. 1; 17. 6; 33. 6). Sinai is the general word, but occurs only once in Deut. (33. 2). said. See note on 2. 9.
thick darkness. See Ex. 20. 21, and cp. Heb. 'araphel. 2 Sam. 22. 10. 1 Kings 8. 12. Ps. 97. 2.

spake. See note on 2. 1. saw. Fig. Zeugma. Ap. 6. i.: by which one verb "saw" is used with two objects and suits only the first. A second verb "heard" must be supplied: cp. Ex. 3. 16. 2 Kings 11. 12. 1 Tim. 4. 3. It is for the purpose of calling attention to the emphasis thus put on the verb "saw"; an idol being that which is seen. similitude = appearance of form, or likeness.
even ten. Heb. the ten. wrote. See note on Ex. 17. 14; only here and 10. 4 in Deut. See also Ap. 47.
me. Emphasis on "me" to call attention to the mediation of Moses.
yourselves = your souls. Heb. nephesh. See v. 9 above and Ap. 13.
graven image. Heb. pesel = a sculpture (Ex. 20. 4). figure. Heb. semel = only here, 2 Chron. 33. 7, 15, and Ezek. 8. 3, 5. likeness = form. Heb. tablinith = model.
host of heaven: sun, moon, and stars. This sin foreknown. 2 Kings 17. 18; 23. 4. Cp. Amos 5. 26 with Acts 7. 42, 43.
iron furnace. Cp. Gen. 15. 17. Ex. 3. 2, 3. 1 Kings 8. 51-53. Jer. 11. 4. to be, &c. Cp. Ex. 19. 5. Deut. 9. 29; 32. 9.

23-40 (r, p. 243). WARNINGS AGAINST IDOLATRY (Alternation). forbidden thee. Heb. zivvah, a Homonym = to command, and to forbid. Here it = forbid, also in Judg. 13. 14, where it is wrongly rendered "command".
a consuming fire. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. Cp. Ex. 24. 17. Heb. 12. 29. GOD. Heb. 'El. See Ap. 4. children = sons.
evil. Heb. ra'a'. Ap. 44. viii.

I call. Fig. Deasis. Ap. 6. Cp. 31. 28. heaven and earth = the heavens and the earth (always plural and with Heb. particle 'eth, except Gen. 2. 1. See note on 1. 1). One of the thirteen occurrences of the Heb. expressions noted in the Massorah. Gen. 1. 1. Ex. 20. 11; 31. 17. Deut. 4. 26; 30. 19; 31. 28. 2 Kings 19. 15. 2 Chron. 2. 12. Isa. 37. 16. Jer. 23. 24; 32. 17. Hag. 2. 6, 21. this day. A solemn idiom, used for great emphasis. Occurs forty-two times (see Ap. 10) in this book: 4. 26, 39, 40; 5. 1; 6. 6; 7. 11; 8. 1, 11, 19; 9. 1, 3; 10. 13; 11. 2, 8, 13, 26, 27, 28, 32; 13. 18; 15. 5, 15; 19. 9; 26. 3, 16, 17, 18; 27. 1, 4, 10; 28. 1, 13, 14, 15; 30. 2, 8, 11, 15, 16, 18, 19; 32. 46. It is this Old Testament idiom in Luke 23. 43. destroyed = exterminated. Heb. shmad.

scatter. Heb. puz = disperse. See Gen. 10. 18; 11. 4, 9, not used in Lev. 26. 33, but is used in Jer. 30. 11, and frequently: also in Ezek. Cp. Deut. 28. 64, and Ezek. 20. 23. nations = peoples. heathen = nations.
serve gods. Cp. Dan 5. 23. Rev. 9. 20. men's. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. I.
thou shalt. This agrees with the Sam. Text., but the printed Heb. Text has "ye shall". seek. Cp. Lev. 26. 40. Jer. 29. 13, &c. soul. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13.
the latter days = the end of the days.

He will not forsake. First occurrence of this promise. Repeated in 31. 6 for the journey. Repeated to Joshua for conflict, Josh. 1. 5, 6; to Solomon for work, 1 Chron. 28. 20; to us for daily provision and comfort, Heb. 13. 5, 6.

the days. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, put for the events which took place in them. created (sing.). These two words occur together three times (Gen. 1. 1; 2. 3, and here). man = Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. I.
Did ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. God: or, a god. as = according as.

hath ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. God: or, a god. from the midst. Here we have the whole of Exodus, cp. Jer. 32. 21. temptations = trials, or, provings. and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), in this verse. war = fightings. Ex. 14. 25.
He is God. Cp. 1 Kings 18. 39. Isa. 45. 21.
God. Heb. ha-'elohim = the God.
for ever = all the days: i.e. for all time.

Then. Emphatic, marking the end of his first address. Moses. Change to third person, not because it is now editorial, but because the first direct address is ended. See note on 1. 1. severed = separated. Cp. Ex. 21. 13. Num. 35. 6-29.
hated = he hated.
4. 44—5. 32 (N, p. 243). STATUTES RECITED. (Alternation.) this: i.e. which hereafter followeth. The commencement of the new section according to the Structure. children = sons.
testimonies. Heb. 'ud, to say again and again, hence, testifyings, affirmations, &c. statutes, and the judgments. See note on 4. 1.
smote. Cp. Num. 21. 24. Deut. 1. 4.
of Og. Cp. Num. 21. 33. Deut. 3. 3.
Sion. Written for Sirion. See Deut. 3. 9.
on this side = across: a neutral term. Cp. 1. 1.
Moses called. Here begins his second address. See note on 1. 1. statutes and judgments. See note on 4. 1. this day. See note on 4. 26. keep, and do = observe to do.

The LORD our God. Jehovah our 'Elohim. made. Heb. cut, because covenants were made by cutting the sacrifice in twain and passing between the parts. See Gen. 15. 10. Jer. 34. 18, 19. Heb. 9. 16, 17. Gal. 3. 20, the latter referring to the one of the two necessary parties to a covenant.
our fathers = our fathers only. us, even us. Fig. Epizeuxis, Ap. 6, well rendered.
talked. Cp. Ex. 19. 19, 20.
I stood. Cp. Ex. 20. 19. saying. Cp. Ex. 20. 1-17.
bondage = Heb. servants, put for servitude.
graven image. Heb. pesel, a sculpture. First occurrence is Ex. 20. 4. See note on 4. 16. likeness = form.
GOD. Heb. 'El. See Ap. 4. IV. iniquity. Heb. 'avah. Ap. 44. iv.
mercy = kindness.
as = according as.
labour. This word is emphasised by the Heb. accent zarha, to show that the fourth Commandment is twofold, and that the one day's rest cannot be enjoyed without the preceding six days of labour.
And remember. A parenthetical break in Moses' recital, in view of their shortly having servants of their own. through = by.
or. Fig. Paradiastole. Ap. 6. his ox. Some codices, with Sept. and Syr., read "or his ox".
spake. See note on 2. 1. wrote. See note on Ex. 17. 14; and Ap. 47. in = on.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. man. Heb. 'adam. Ap. 14. I.
why ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
who ...? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. the living God. Both plurals. First occurrence of this title, always in contrast with idols, latent or expressed. Cp. Acts 14. 15. 1 Thess. 1. 9, &c.
said. See note on 2. 9.
O that, &c. Fig. Oeonismos. Ap. 6. always = every day, or all the days.
commandments. Heb. pl. "all the commandment", i.e. this whole Law. statutes, and the judgments. See note on 4. 1.

6. 1—11. 25 (b, p. 219). INJUNCTIONS ON ENTRY INTO LAND (Introversion and Alternations). these are. Heb. "this is". commandments. See note on 5. 31. statutes, and the judgments. See note on 4. 1. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. II. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. I. go. Heb. pass over.

Hear ... observe. Note the Fig. Paronomasia (Ap. 6), used for emphasis: v'shama'ta ... v'shamarta. May be Englished "Hear ... Heed". as = according as. the land, &c. Cp. Gen. 17. 8. Ex. 3. 8, 17; 13. 5; 33. 3. Num. 13. 27; 14. 8; 16. 13, 14. Josh. 5. 6. Jer. 11. 5; 32. 22. Ezek. 20. 6, 15.

Hear.
